source.citation: Jack Challoner (ed.), "1,001 Inventions That Changed the World", Cassell Illustrated / Chartwell Books, various editions
source.note: This file is a preliminary, unreviewed extraction of all 1,001 numbered chapters in the book (8 chronological parts). Unlike the Haven seed file, each entry here was produced by reading that chapter's own short text (its stated date, one-line tagline, and 2-3 paragraphs of historical context), not just a table-of-contents title, so bookStatedDate, category, and possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion are grounded in the book's own wording rather than guessed from the title alone. Page numbers (sourcePage) were read from each chapter's page-break marker; where a chapter had none (because it starts partway down a page shared with the previous chapter), the page number was forward-filled from the nearest preceding chapter that had one, so treat sourcePage as approximate in those cases. Nothing here should be treated as authoritative or complete. Categories and social-adjustment questions are this project's own draft judgment calls, not the book's own framing, and every entry is candidateStatus "unreviewed" until checked by a human against this project's case-eligibility rules and, where a full case is built, against sources beyond this one book.
source.candidateStatusMeaning: unreviewed means the entry has not been checked against other sources or against this project's case-eligibility rules, even though its category and question were grounded in the book's own chapter text.
source.notableForFullCaseMeaning: A rough triage flag set during extraction: true means the chapter text itself described a specific, concrete episode of adoption, resistance, competition, or consequence, worth a closer look as a possible full case. False does not mean unimportant, only that this particular chapter's text did not supply that kind of material on its own. About 24 percent of entries are flagged true.
source.extractionMethod: Extracted by 8 parallel research passes, one per book part, each reading every chapter file directly rather than relying on titles alone.

candidates.title: Stone Tools
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once early humans could shape stone into reliable cutting and hacking tools?
candidates.notes: The first human invention: purposely sharpened stone tools that made hunting, butchering, and shelter-building far more effective.

candidates.title: Controlled Fire
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once humans could keep fire burning rather than merely encounter it by chance?
candidates.notes: Controlling fire let early humans keep warm, cook, ward off predators, clear land, and eventually smelt metal.

candidates.title: Built Shelter
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once early hominids could build shelter rather than rely on caves alone?
candidates.notes: Homo heidelbergensis built some of the earliest known huts, letting people live near food and water and freeing up time to experiment.

candidates.title: Clothing
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once humans could clothe themselves against the environment?
candidates.notes: Early humans made clothing from fur and leaves, a technology whose role as a status and identity marker has persisted ever since.

candidates.title: Spear
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once early hominids could sharpen and fire-harden a simple wooden pole into a weapon?
candidates.notes: The sharpened, fire-hardened spear gave early hunters a more effective way to bring down prey like mammoths.

candidates.title: Fishhook
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once early humans could reliably retain fish they caught rather than lose them?
candidates.notes: Early bone, shell, and wood fishhooks gave prehistoric people easy access to a protein-rich food source, freeing time for other activities.

candidates.title: Tally Stick
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Who had to adjust once medieval England's Exchequer began recording tax payments as physical, split tally sticks?
candidates.notes: Notched tally sticks recorded numbers and, in medieval England, became the split, forgery-resistant instrument for tracking royal tax payments.

candidates.title: Drill
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once humans had a dedicated tool for boring holes into wood, bone, and later metal?
candidates.notes: Early humans adapted a modified spear into a drill, later refined by Egyptian woodworkers into the bow drill.

candidates.title: Sharp Stone Blade
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once toolmakers mastered lithic reduction to control the sharpness and shape of stone blades?
candidates.notes: Deliberate flintknapping techniques let Stone Age humans produce increasingly sophisticated, purpose-built stone blades.

candidates.title: Sewing
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once early humans could sew rather than merely drape hides and leaves?
candidates.notes: Bone and ivory needles let early humans tailor clothing closely to the body, improving insulation and enabling decoration.

candidates.title: Atlatl
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once hunters could throw a dart with more force than the human arm alone could generate?
candidates.notes: The atlatl used leverage and stored energy to hurl darts at very high speed, and may have contributed to the extinction of the woolly mammoth.

candidates.title: Bow and Arrow
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once hunters could strike prey from outside their own throwing range?
candidates.notes: The bow and arrow was the first machine to store muscular energy and release it as projectile force, extending the hunter's reach.

candidates.title: Boomerang
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once a thrown weapon could be designed to return to the thrower?
candidates.notes: The boomerang evolved from simpler throwing sticks and clubs into a specialized hunting and, among some peoples, recreational tool.

candidates.title: Braided Rope
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once humans could braid fibers into rope strong enough to anchor, tie, and haul?
candidates.notes: Braided rope let people carry prey, move huge stones, and eventually rig sailing ships, produced for centuries in dedicated roperies.

candidates.title: Lunar Calendar
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once people could track time by recording the phases of the moon?
candidates.notes: The earliest known lunar calendar, marked in a French cave, let early humans track the moon's cycle for religious and seasonal purposes.

candidates.title: Alcoholic Drink
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Who had to adjust once alcoholic drink shifted from a status symbol among the wealthy to a commercially produced, sometimes prohibited, commodity?
candidates.notes: Fermented drinks go back to the Neolithic and have swung between status symbol, economic staple, and, during U.S. Prohibition, a banned substance.

candidates.title: Pottery
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once nomadic hunter-gatherers, not just settled farmers, were found to have invented fired pottery?
candidates.notes: Japanese hunter-gatherers fired clay into pots roughly a thousand years before similar sun-dried pots appeared in the Near East.

candidates.title: Oil Lamp
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once humans could produce controlled, portable light after dark?
candidates.notes: The oil lamp let people see, work, and perform rituals at night for millennia, until gas and electric lighting made it obsolete.

candidates.title: Sling
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once a simple pouch and cord could hurl a stone farther than any human arm?
candidates.notes: The sling was cheap, portable, and effective, becoming common everywhere in the ancient world except Australia.

candidates.title: Granary
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once early farmers could store surplus grain through the granary rather than consume it immediately?
candidates.notes: The world's first known granary, at Dhra' in the Jordan Valley, let early farmers store surplus food, supporting population growth but narrowing dietary variety.

candidates.title: Metalworking
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once humans could extract and shape metal rather than rely only on stone and bone?
candidates.notes: Metalworking began with a copper pendant around 8700 BCE and progressed through smelting, alloying, and eventually the Bronze and Iron Ages.

candidates.title: Dugout Canoe
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once people could hollow out a log to travel on water rather than swim or cling to driftwood?
candidates.notes: The dugout canoe, made by burning and scraping out a log, was the earliest known form of boat.

candidates.title: Chisel
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once toolmakers had a dedicated chisel rather than general-purpose stone tools for carving?
candidates.notes: The chisel evolved from Paleolithic stone tools into a standard carving and carpentry implement used from ancient Greece through the medieval period.

candidates.title: Dried Brick
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once builders could mold and dry portable mud bricks rather than build with whatever stone was at hand?
candidates.notes: Dried mud bricks let people build houses, granaries, and eventually whole cities wherever stone was scarce.

candidates.title: Sledge
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once people could haul heavy loads across snow and ice rather than carry them by hand?
candidates.notes: The sledge let Arctic and later other peoples transport large loads, eventually pulled by dogs, oxen, and even kites.

candidates.title: Fort
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about warfare and defense as fortifications evolved from hillforts to underground bunkers?
candidates.notes: Communal defensive forts evolved for millennia in response to changing weapons, from cannons to explosive shells to mobile tank warfare.

candidates.title: Travois
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once nomadic peoples could drag loads across soft soil where sleds and carts failed?
candidates.notes: The travois, a dragged A-frame, let Native Americans move belongings, and occasionally the sick or elderly, across terrain unsuited to sleds or carts.

candidates.title: Shoe
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What social customs developed once humans began covering their feet rather than going barefoot?
candidates.notes: Early shoes protected feet from the ground, and over time gave rise to customs about when and where shoes are removed.

candidates.title: Woven Cloth
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once fibers could be woven on a loom rather than felted or draped?
candidates.notes: Weaving, first evidenced at Çatalhöyük, led to warmer, more durable, and more varied textile products than felt alone allowed.

candidates.title: Map
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once people could represent the wider world on a map rather than know only what they had personally traveled?
candidates.notes: Early maps ranged from a Çatalhöyük town plan to Ptolemy's world guide, whose underestimate of the Earth's size later misled Columbus about the distance to India.

candidates.title: Wattle and Daub
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once builders could weatherproof wooden house frames with woven wattle and mud daub?
candidates.notes: Wattle and daub filled the gaps in timber-framed houses, though damp walls could rot and were notoriously easy to break through.

candidates.title: Irrigation
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once farmers could bring water to fields artificially rather than depend on rain alone?
candidates.notes: Irrigation channels and reservoirs let early farmers extend fertile land far beyond riverbanks, supporting larger and more reliable harvests.

candidates.title: Axe
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did the axe make possible once it could be hafted onto a handle for controlled, repeated use?
candidates.notes: The hafted axe helped clear rainforest for agriculture and, buried with the dead, became a symbol of high social rank.

candidates.title: Scratch Plow
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once farmers had a tool to aerate soil and cut furrows rather than plant by hand?
candidates.notes: The Mesopotamian scratch plow let farmers prepare larger areas of land for planting than manual methods allowed.

candidates.title: Plaster
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Who had to adjust once a French king mandated that Paris's wooden houses be coated in plaster as fire protection?
candidates.notes: Plaster of gypsum served as mortar, decorative surface, and eventually a fire-safety mandate for the wooden houses of Paris.

candidates.title: Toothpaste
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did people believe caused tooth pain before dental hygiene practices were grounded in anything beyond myth and superstition?
candidates.notes: Egyptian tooth-cleaning pastes of abrasive minerals gave way to centuries of superstition before scientific dentifrice emerged in the 1800s.

candidates.title: Carpentry
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once humans could deliberately shape wood into complex forms rather than use it as found?
candidates.notes: Carpentry grew from basic tool use into a distinct craft as Neolithic peoples settled into permanent timber dwellings.

candidates.title: Rowboat
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once Mesopotamians could propel boats with paddles rather than drift with the current alone?
candidates.notes: Rowing let reed boats travel upstream against the Tigris and Euphrates rivers, complementing river travel by animal towing.

candidates.title: Canal
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for canal-borne trade once railroads offered a faster alternative?
candidates.notes: Artificial waterways moved goods cheaply for millennia, but British canals fell into decline for over a century once railroads arrived.

candidates.title: Glue
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once broken objects could be mended, and separate materials joined, with adhesive?
candidates.notes: Glue made from tree sap, birch tar, and animal products let ancient peoples repair pottery and craft composite objects.

candidates.title: Log-laid Road
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once logs could be laid to create a passable road over swampy or muddy terrain?
candidates.notes: Corduroy roads opened travel through otherwise impassable land, though a bumpy and hazardous ride was often the cost.

candidates.title: Rivet
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What consequences can follow when a small fastening component like the rivet is made from substandard material?
candidates.notes: Rivets have joined metal since ancient Egypt, and researchers have blamed substandard iron rivets for the Titanic's fatal 1912 sinking.

candidates.title: Wheel and Axle
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once the potter's wheel and the sledge combined into a wheel-and-axle for transport?
candidates.notes: The wheel evolved from the potter's wheel and the sledge, enabling carts, wagons, and chariots to carry loads efficiently.

candidates.title: Plywood
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once scarce fine wood could be stretched by gluing thin decorative veneers onto cheaper wood?
candidates.notes: Plywood began as an economical, cosmetic solution in wood-poor Egypt and later proved structurally stronger than solid wood.

candidates.title: Lubricating Grease
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once wheeled vehicles could be lubricated to reduce friction and wear?
candidates.notes: Lubricating grease made from olive oil and animal fat kept ancient wheels, and later steam engines, running smoothly.

candidates.title: Cart
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once loads could be carried on wheels rather than dragged?
candidates.notes: The cart, developed alongside the wheel, has persisted in forms from horse-drawn wagons to the modern shopping cart.

candidates.title: Sail
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once sailors could angle a sail to catch wind from more than one direction?
candidates.notes: Sails let Egyptian and Phoenician vessels harness wind power, eventually enabling ships to sail nearly into the wind itself.

candidates.title: Oven
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once bread could be baked in an enclosed oven rather than only as flatbread?
candidates.notes: The Egyptian closed oven let bakers produce leavened, risen bread rather than flatbread alone.

candidates.title: Flail
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did the flail's role as a pharaonic symbol reveal about the link between grain and political power?
candidates.notes: The flail separated grain from chaff and, held by Egyptian pharaohs alongside the shepherd's crook, symbolized the ruler's duty to feed the people.

candidates.title: Bell
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did the bell come to signal to a community once it moved from pottery instrument to symbol of imperial power?
candidates.notes: Chinese bells evolved from tuned clay instruments to bronze ritual bells and eventually a symbol of dynastic authority.

candidates.title: Candle
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once a wick could draw fuel steadily to produce a constant, controllable flame?
candidates.notes: The candle offered constant artificial light for millennia until paraffin, gas, and electricity displaced its practical role.

candidates.title: Pliers
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once metal tongs for handling hot coals evolved into a precise gripping tool?
candidates.notes: Pliers evolved from fire-handling tongs into metal gripping tools once iron forging became common.

candidates.title: Investment Casting
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once metalworkers could cast a single object with intricate detail using a wax mold?
candidates.notes: Lost-wax investment casting let ancient Egyptians and Mesopotamians produce detailed idols and jewelry, a technique still used for precision parts.

candidates.title: Button
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened to the button's power as a status symbol once mass production made it cheap and common?
candidates.notes: Buttons shifted from Bronze Age ornament to a fastener that became a display of wealth for the rich, before mass production diminished their status value.

candidates.title: Helmet
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once soldiers could protect the head with a fitted metal helmet?
candidates.notes: Helmets began as Mesopotamian and Egyptian war gear and later specialized far beyond combat, into cycling and space exploration.

candidates.title: Ski
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once hunters could stay atop snow rather than sink into it?
candidates.notes: Skis let the Lapps and other northern peoples hunt and travel efficiently across ice-covered terrain.

candidates.title: Ice Skate
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once travelers could cross frozen lakes on bone-bladed skates rather than wait for spring?
candidates.notes: Ice skates solved a real transportation problem in lake-dense Finland, where villages were often cut off by frozen water each winter.

candidates.title: Cuneiform
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once Sumerians could record economic transactions in writing rather than with physical tokens?
candidates.notes: Cuneiform, humankind's first writing system, let Sumerians move beyond counting tokens to a full written record of trade, law, and thought.

candidates.title: Dam
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once societies could deliberately block a river's flow with a constructed dam?
candidates.notes: Dams evolved from a failed Egyptian earth-and-rubble structure into Roman arch dams and eventually vast hydroelectric projects.

candidates.title: Chair
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once a stool gained a back to support the seated body?
candidates.notes: Egyptian craftsmen added a back to the stool, gradually developing the high-back, then padded and armed, chair.

candidates.title: Soap
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once fats and ashes could be combined into a reliable emulsifying agent for cleaning?
candidates.notes: Babylonian soap recipes, preserved on clay cylinders, worked by trapping dirt and grease inside micelles that could be washed away.

candidates.title: Arched Bridge
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once builders could distribute weight through a curved arch rather than a straight beam?
candidates.notes: The arch let builders create longer, stronger bridges by transferring load sideways through wedge-shaped voussoirs to the abutments.

candidates.title: Brazing and Soldering
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once metalworkers could join pieces of metal without fully melting either one?
candidates.notes: Brazing and soldering used a lower-melting filler metal to join pieces without the whole-piece melting that welding required.

candidates.title: Glass
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once the blowpipe made glass cheap enough to be more than a luxury item?
candidates.notes: Glass began as an Egyptian luxury good and spread throughout the Roman Empire once the blowpipe lowered its cost of production.

candidates.title: Welding
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once metalworkers could hammer-weld iron particles together by expelling molten slag?
candidates.notes: Forge welding, evidenced in an Anatolian tomb, remained the only known joining technique for iron for centuries.

candidates.title: Bellows
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once furnace fires could be stoked by bellows rather than human breath alone?
candidates.notes: Bellows let smelters reach far higher furnace temperatures than blowpipes, eventually making iron smelting possible for the first time.

candidates.title: Flush Toilet
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Why did John Harrington's 1596 water closet fail to catch on even though it worked?
candidates.notes: Water-flushed toilets existed in the Indus Valley by 2500 BCE, but a working design invented in Renaissance England went largely unadopted for nearly two centuries.

candidates.title: Sewage System
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What health consequences persisted for centuries once early sewage technology was left unimproved in Western European cities?
candidates.notes: Indus Valley brick-lined sewer networks predated later cities, but inadequate sewage systems in Western Europe still caused fatal cholera and typhoid outbreaks as late as the nineteenth century.

candidates.title: Pesticide
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once insects developed immunity to DDT after its wartime success against mosquito-borne disease?
candidates.notes: Sumerian sulfur was the earliest known chemical pesticide, but reliance on chemical agents like DDT later provoked toxicity fears and a turn back toward organic methods.

candidates.title: Standard Measures
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became governable in trade once merchants could rely on a standardized system of weights?
candidates.notes: The Indus Valley Civilization developed doubling cube weights for fair trade, while Mesopotamia relied on carved stone 'sleeping goose' standards instead.

candidates.title: Wrought Iron
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once smiths could reduce iron ore to workable iron without fully melting it?
candidates.notes: Wrought iron, the material that gave the Iron Age its name, was eventually overtaken by cheaper, stronger steel.

candidates.title: Ink
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once a pigment could be fixed into a liquid that dried permanently onto a surface?
candidates.notes: Chinese ink, first used to emphasize carved lettering, evolved into stick inks and eventually specialized inks for writing and printing.

candidates.title: Enclosed Harbor
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once traders could load and unload cargo at a purpose-built, enclosed harbor?
candidates.notes: The Lothal dock connected Indus Valley trade to distant Mesopotamian goods before flooding buried it in silt.

candidates.title: Tunnel
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once a besieged city could dig a tunnel to secure a water supply the enemy couldn't cut off?
candidates.notes: Hezekiah's Tunnel was excavated through solid rock from both ends to bring water into Jerusalem ahead of an Assyrian siege.

candidates.title: Water Filter
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What had to be discovered about invisible contaminants before clear-tasting water was recognized as potentially dangerous?
candidates.notes: Ancient filtration judged water purity by taste and appearance until an 1855 London cholera outbreak traced to contaminated water proved invisible contaminants could cause disease.

candidates.title: Mechanical Lock
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What ongoing contest began once mechanical locks were invented to keep intruders out of a home or building?
candidates.notes: Egyptian pin-based locks began a centuries-long back-and-forth between locksmiths protecting property and lock pickers defeating them.

candidates.title: Anesthesia
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once a substance first used as a party amusement came to be seen as a legitimate way to control surgical pain?
candidates.notes: Ancient Egyptians and Assyrians limited pain with blood-flow restriction and herbal mixtures, but nitrous oxide was treated as recreational entertainment for decades before a U.S. dentist used it for painless extractions.

candidates.title: Spoked-wheel Chariot
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in warfare once bronze technology allowed a lighter, spoked wheel to replace the heavy solid wheel?
candidates.notes: The spoked-wheel chariot let a charioteer outpace foot soldiers while a warrior attacked with speed and maneuverability.

candidates.title: Fired Brick
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once bricks could be kiln-fired rather than left to dry, and potentially dissolve, in the sun?
candidates.notes: Fired brick let builders construct permanent structures far more resilient to rain and weathering than sun-dried mud brick.

candidates.title: Saw
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once cutting blades could be fitted with metal teeth rather than relying on stone edges?
candidates.notes: The metal-toothed saw let Egyptian and later craftsmen cut wood and metal more precisely than earlier stone tools allowed.

candidates.title: Alphabet
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Who could record their own thoughts once a simplified phonetic alphabet replaced complex hieroglyphic writing?
candidates.notes: The oldest known phonetic alphabet, found as graffiti in Egypt's western desert, let ordinary soldiers and people record names and thoughts, and underlies nearly every alphabet used today.

candidates.title: Umbrella
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Who resisted the umbrella, and why, before it lost its association with femininity in eighteenth-century England?
candidates.notes: The umbrella shielded monarchs from the sun for millennia, but in England it faced resistance from religious objectors and carriage drivers before shedding its gendered image.

candidates.title: Quernstone
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once grain could be ground into flour using two stones rather than eaten or processed whole?
candidates.notes: The quernstone let settled farming communities grind grain into flour, eventually evolving into water- and wind-powered mills.

candidates.title: Aqueduct
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once water could be conveyed artificially to places without a reliable natural supply?
candidates.notes: Aqueducts, developed first in water-scarce Minoan Crete, let the Romans and later industrial cities supply water beyond local sources.

candidates.title: Rubber Ball
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What was at stake for players once a processed rubber ball became central to a ritual game with political and religious significance?
candidates.notes: Mesoamerican rubber balls were used in ritual games whose losing captain could be sacrificed, making the invention part of a life-and-death political and religious institution.

candidates.title: Shadow Clock
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once time could be tracked from the length and direction of a cast shadow?
candidates.notes: The Egyptian shadow clock divided daylight into hours using a portable T-shaped device aligned to the cardinal directions.

candidates.title: Scissors
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once fabric could be cut precisely with a pivoted, spring-connected blade?
candidates.notes: Spring-type scissors, used in Egypt for cutting silhouettes, evolved through Roman pivoted designs into mass-produced steel scissors.

candidates.title: Water Clock
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once time could be measured from a steady flow of water rather than the visible sun and stars?
candidates.notes: The water clock let Egyptians, and later Romans and Chinese, keep time even when clouds hid the sun and stars.

candidates.title: Steel
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once controlled amounts of carbon could be added to iron to harden it?
candidates.notes: Steel, first produced in sub-Saharan East Africa, let smiths tune hardness against brittleness, culminating in famed Damascan blades.

candidates.title: Sword
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once iron smelting allowed blades longer than bronze could practically support?
candidates.notes: Iron smelting let swordsmiths produce longer blades than bronze allowed, and the sword's design kept evolving through the eighteenth century.

candidates.title: Rudder
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once ships could be steered from the stern rather than relying only on oars and wind?
candidates.notes: The rudder let sailors redirect water flow past the hull to steer, eventually enabling the rise of Western naval fleets.

candidates.title: Abacus
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once large numbers could be calculated accurately on a frame of sliding beads rather than fingers?
candidates.notes: The abacus, developed from a Mesopotamian counting board, let people calculate and record numbers far larger than finger-counting allowed.

candidates.title: Pontoon Bridge
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once a river crossing could be built quickly from floating pontoons rather than fixed construction?
candidates.notes: The pontoon bridge, first built for a royal wedding procession, became a fast, if vulnerable, way to cross rivers for both ceremony and war.

candidates.title: Battering Ram
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What defensive adjustments did fortified towns make once besiegers could swing a covered, wheeled battering ram at their walls?
candidates.notes: The Assyrian battering ram, suspended in a protective wooden frame, could breach fortifications that earlier hand-carried rams could not.

candidates.title: Sandwich
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What legal and cultural disputes has the sandwich's simple format provoked over what actually counts as one?
candidates.notes: The sandwich, with roots from Hittite ration bread to a Jewish Passover tradition, was popularized in England by the Earl of Sandwich as a food he could eat without dirtying his hands at cards.

candidates.title: Inoculation
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Who was willing to be inoculated with weakened smallpox material before the practice was proven safe enough for the royal family?
candidates.notes: Chinese variolation, which ground scabs from smallpox survivors for inoculation, was first tested on condemned prisoners in London before the royal family adopted it and made it fashionable.

candidates.title: Kite
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once a lightweight frame of silk and bamboo could be flown on a string?
candidates.notes: Chinese kites were used to measure distances, test wind, and send military signals, and later helped Franklin and the Wright brothers with scientific experiments.

candidates.title: Pulley
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once a wheel and rope could change the direction, and later multiply the force, of a pull?
candidates.notes: The pulley let people move or lift loads more easily, and compound pulley systems could multiply the applied force many times over.

candidates.title: Buckle
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once clothing and equipment could be fastened with a buckle rather than laces alone?
candidates.notes: The buckle offered a durable fastening solution that solved practical problems from armor to, reportedly, a British sailor's waterlogged trousers.

candidates.title: Metal Anchor
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once anchors could be weighted and shaped from metal rather than stone or sand?
candidates.notes: Metal anchors, developed as ships grew larger, let sailors moor more reliably than the stones and sandbags used before.

candidates.title: Crossbow
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Who condemned the crossbow as dishonorable, and why, even as it let untrained soldiers kill armored knights?
candidates.notes: The Chinese crossbow let an unskilled soldier injure or kill an armored knight, provoking condemnation as an inhuman weapon from critics including the Pope in 1139.

candidates.title: Crane
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once cranes could multiply human lifting power through pulleys and mechanical advantage?
candidates.notes: Cranes let ancient Greek and Roman builders raise stone blocks weighing many tons far higher than human strength alone allowed.

candidates.title: Artificial Limb
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did it mean for a wounded soldier or amputee to return to daily life, or even to battle, with a fashioned prosthetic limb?
candidates.notes: Ancient prosthetic limbs, from a Roman general's iron hand to the Capua leg, let amputees return to normal activity, and even combat.

candidates.title: Winch
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once a cleated winch could hold tension on a rope or cable without constant human effort?
candidates.notes: The winch, first used to tighten bridge cables, became essential for construction, mooring, torture devices, and helicopter rescue alike.

candidates.title: Hammock
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once sailors could sleep in a bed that moved in harmony with a rolling ship?
candidates.notes: The hammock, adopted by Europeans after Columbus encountered it in the Caribbean, became standard issue for sailors within a century.

candidates.title: Chain Mail
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once armor could be woven from interlinked metal rings rather than solid plates?
candidates.notes: Chain mail offered flexible, lightweight protection against cutting blows, though it needed a padded garment underneath to resist crushing impact.

candidates.title: Distillation
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once chemical substances could be separated from a mixture by controlled boiling and condensation?
candidates.notes: Distillation, understood early for alcohol, was later applied to purifying water and, centuries afterward, extracting pure chemical substances.

candidates.title: Pike
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What military advantage did the Macedonian phalanx gain once soldiers could strike with pikes from beyond their enemies' reach?
candidates.notes: Philip II's pike and phalanx formation gave Macedonia a battlefield advantage that Alexander the Great used to conquer Egypt, Persia, and northern India.

candidates.title: Magnetic Compass
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Why did it take roughly a thousand years for the magnetic compass to move from quasi-magical uses to actual navigation?
candidates.notes: The Chinese discovered lodestone's orientation effect around the fourth century BCE, but used it for quasi-magical purposes for about a millennium before adopting it for navigation.

candidates.title: Blast Furnace
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once furnaces could sustain the heat needed to smelt cast iron on a larger scale?
candidates.notes: The Chinese blast furnace, evolved from bronze-melting furnaces, eventually let iron production scale up across medieval Europe.

candidates.title: Catapult
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did it mean for siege warfare once attackers could launch disease, not just stones, over castle walls?
candidates.notes: Catapults hurled stones and bolts at fortifications, and were sometimes loaded with beehives or animal carcasses to infect those inside.

candidates.title: Stirrup
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in mounted warfare once riders had a stable footing to fight from rather than balance alone?
candidates.notes: The stirrup, which began as a simple mounting aid in China, fundamentally altered mounted combat and accelerated cultural contact and migration.

candidates.title: Saddle
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for riders once a padded, framed saddle offered comfort that folded blankets and bareback riding could not?
candidates.notes: The padded saddle, developed in Han China, became both a comfort improvement and a status symbol before the stirrup completed its usefulness.

candidates.title: Moldboard Plow
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once a plow blade could turn the soil over rather than merely scratch a furrow?
candidates.notes: The Chinese moldboard plow buried weeds and brought nutrients to the surface, letting much larger areas be farmed efficiently.

candidates.title: Lever
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once the mechanics of a pivoted bar could be understood and deliberately applied to lifting?
candidates.notes: Archimedes formally described the lever, though Egyptians had already used the principle for weighing and for devices like the shaduf.

candidates.title: Nail
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Why were handmade nails once valuable enough that people would burn down their own houses to retrieve them?
candidates.notes: Early forged nails were so costly and labor-intensive to produce that people reportedly burned their houses when moving just to salvage the nails for reuse.

candidates.title: Archimedes Screw
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once water could be lifted continuously up a spiral tube rather than carried by hand?
candidates.notes: The Archimedes screw raised water for irrigation and mining, and centuries later helped the Netherlands reclaim land from the sea.

candidates.title: Compound Pulley
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once multiple pulleys could be mounted on a single axle to multiply lifting force?
candidates.notes: Archimedes's compound pulley, or block and tackle, reportedly let him move a warship single-handedly and remains standard lifting equipment today.

candidates.title: Pipe Organ
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once air pressure could be mechanically regulated to keep organ pipes sounding steadily?
candidates.notes: Ktesibios's hydraulis used pressurized water to supply steady air to organ pipes, producing a sound loud enough for outdoor games and processions.

candidates.title: Dry Dock
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once a ship's hull could be worked on out of the water rather than only launched or repaired afloat?
candidates.notes: The dry dock let shipbuilders and repairers drain water from around a vessel, a practice that began in Ptolemaic Egypt.

candidates.title: Windmill
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once wind power could be mechanically converted into grinding or pumping force?
candidates.notes: Windmills, used in China and Persia to pump water and mill grain, eventually spread across Europe for centuries before steam and electricity took over.

candidates.title: Astrolabe
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for Muslim travelers once the astrolabe let them calculate prayer times and the direction of Mecca from the stars?
candidates.notes: Hipparchus's astronomical projection became the astrolabe, later prized in the Islamic world for determining prayer times and the direction of Mecca.

candidates.title: Antikythera Mechanism
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What does it mean that a 2,000-year-old Greek mechanism encoded a heliocentric model of the solar system not otherwise accepted at the time?
candidates.notes: The Antikythera Mechanism, recovered from a shipwreck, calculated astronomical positions using gearing complexity not matched again until eighteenth-century clocks.

candidates.title: Parchment
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened once a rival library's papyrus supply was allegedly cut off, forcing Pergamum to develop parchment instead?
candidates.notes: Parchment, made from scraped animal skin, may have been developed after Egypt stopped exporting papyrus to a rival library, and it eventually enabled sewn books rather than scrolls.

candidates.title: Belt Drive
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once rotating shafts could be linked by a belt to transfer power between them?
candidates.notes: The belt drive, first used with a treadmill-powered Roman crane, went on to distribute power throughout factories and modern engines alike.

candidates.title: Watermill
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once flowing water could be harnessed mechanically to grind grain rather than relying on human or animal power?
candidates.notes: The watermill evolved from a Greek vertical-axis design into a source of industrial and, eventually, hydroelectric power.

candidates.title: Blown Glass
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once molten glass could be shaped by blowing air through a tube rather than only molded or cast?
candidates.notes: Glassblowing let Syrian craftsmen, and later the Romans, shape glass into intricate forms far more easily than earlier techniques allowed.

candidates.title: Odometer
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once distances between places could be measured mechanically rather than by counting footsteps?
candidates.notes: Vitruvius devised a mechanical device to make measuring distances easier.

candidates.title: Ball Bearing
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened when a low-friction industrial technology became valuable enough that nations targeted its factories as a wartime strategy?
candidates.notes: The Romans developed an early method for reducing rotational friction.

candidates.title: Claw Hammer
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for carpenters once a single tool could both drive in and remove valuable nails?
candidates.notes: The Romans created a tool for both driving in and pulling out nails.

candidates.title: Horseshoe
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for transport and warfare once horses' hooves were protected from wear?
candidates.notes: The Romans invented an early horseshoe called the hipposandal.

candidates.title: Dome
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became architecturally possible once engineers could build a self-supporting dome without it collapsing during construction?
candidates.notes: Roman engineers solved the structural puzzle of building a self-supporting dome.

candidates.title: Suspension Bridge
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for travelers once valleys and rivers could be crossed on bridges suspended from chains rather than fixed supports?
candidates.notes: The Chinese built a bridge suspended by iron chains.

candidates.title: Paper
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once a cheap, lightweight writing material spread beyond the empire that tried to keep its production a secret?
candidates.notes: Ts'ai Lun refined and popularized a process for making paper.

candidates.title: Wheelbarrow
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for agriculture and construction once a single person could move loads that once required more labor?
candidates.notes: Zhuge Liang's wheelbarrow made moving heavy loads easier.

candidates.title: Trebuchet
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for besieged towns once attackers could hurl both boulders and disease-bearing corpses over their walls?
candidates.notes: The Chinese developed a counterweight-powered siege weapon.

candidates.title: Horse Collar
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for agriculture once horses could pull far heavier loads without the harness choking them?
candidates.notes: A Chinese padded collar let horses pull much heavier loads without choking.

candidates.title: Quill Pen
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for scribes and the spread of religious texts once feathers became the standard writing tool?
candidates.notes: A Spanish scholar recorded the earliest reference to the quill pen.

candidates.title: Toilet Paper
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did access to different hygiene materials reveal about social class and geography across historical societies?
candidates.notes: The Chinese pioneered the use of paper for personal hygiene.

candidates.title: Spinning Wheel
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in the division of labor once a mechanized wheel sped up thread production ahead of factory-based spinning?
candidates.notes: Indian spinners accelerated thread production with a mechanized wheel.

candidates.title: Tidal Mill
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for millers once tidal flows, rather than unpredictable wind or river current, could power a mill?
candidates.notes: Irish monks built a mill powered by tidal water flow.

candidates.title: Gunpowder
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for warfare and society once an explosive powder spread from Chinese alchemists to Arab armies to European battlefields?
candidates.notes: Chinese alchemists created gunpowder, setting off the race toward firearms.

candidates.title: Banknote
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened to trust in money once a government could issue currency without inherent material value, and what happened when it issued too much?
candidates.notes: The Tang Dynasty introduced paper money to address a copper shortage.

candidates.title: Woodblock Printing
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for the spread of religious texts once a single carved block could stamp out a thousand identical sheets a day?
candidates.notes: Chinese artisans used carved wooden blocks to mass-produce texts and images.

candidates.title: Rocket
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for militaries once fire-propelled arrows spread from a Chinese siege to Mongol, Middle Eastern, and European arsenals?
candidates.notes: Chinese fire arrows using gunpowder marked the beginning of rocketry.

candidates.title: Canal Lock
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for water transport once boats could pass between water levels without wasting the water downstream?
candidates.notes: Qiao Weiyo's pound lock improved canal navigation.

candidates.title: Lens
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once ground and polished glass let people correct their own eyesight rather than accept vision loss?
candidates.notes: Ibn al-Haytham's treatise laid the foundations of optical science.

candidates.title: Sextant
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became measurable once a wall-mounted instrument could pin down a location's latitude to a fraction of a degree?
candidates.notes: Abu-Mahmud al-Khujandi built a giant instrument to measure the sun's altitude.

candidates.title: Movable Type
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Why did reusable type fail to transform Chinese society the way it later transformed Europe under Gutenberg?
candidates.notes: Bi Sheng created reusable clay characters for printing.

candidates.title: Tower Clock
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for tracking time and the heavens once a single water-powered tower could do both mechanically?
candidates.notes: Su Song built an elaborate water-powered astronomical clock tower.

candidates.title: Chain Drive
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for machine design once power could be transmitted precisely through a chain instead of a slipping belt?
candidates.notes: Su Song's clock tower concealed an early endless chain drive.

candidates.title: Cannon
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for fortified cities once bronze and iron cannons could breach walls that had withstood earlier siege weapons?
candidates.notes: The Chinese developed bronze cannons from earlier bamboo fire lances.

candidates.title: Fireworks
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed when gunpowder, first developed for war, was redirected toward festivals and public entertainment?
candidates.notes: The Chinese turned gunpowder into festival explosives.

candidates.title: Arabic Numerals
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became calculable once Europe replaced Roman numerals with a place-value system from India and the Arab world?
candidates.notes: Fibonacci's book popularized Hindu-Arabic numerals in Europe.

candidates.title: Crankshaft
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became mechanically possible once rotary motion could be reliably converted into back-and-forth motion, and vice versa?
candidates.notes: Al-Jazari devised the crankshaft to convert rotary and reciprocating motion.

candidates.title: Camshaft
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for milling, sawing, and later engines once rotational power could be converted into timed mechanical actions?
candidates.notes: Al-Jazari devised the camshaft to transform rotational power into other motion.

candidates.title: Automaton
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once machines could be programmed to repeat complex actions like humans, anticipating today's industrial robots?
candidates.notes: Al-Jazari built an early programmable automaton, a forerunner of today's robots.

candidates.title: Spectacles
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for aging scholars and readers once ground glass lenses could correct both farsightedness and nearsightedness?
candidates.notes: Venetian glassmakers produced some of the first European eyeglasses.

candidates.title: Land Mine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for civilians once buried explosive weapons could keep killing long after a war had ended?
candidates.notes: The Chinese pioneered a concealed, pressure-triggered explosive weapon.

candidates.title: Scythe
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for farm workers and productivity once a standing tool replaced the back-breaking sickle for harvesting?
candidates.notes: A curved-blade tool let European farmworkers harvest standing up, boosting output.

candidates.title: Musket
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened to the social hierarchy of warfare once a weapon let untrained commoners kill armored, highly trained noblemen?
candidates.notes: Chinese gunsmiths' firearm eventually let common soldiers challenge armored noble cavalry.

candidates.title: Production Line
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for shipbuilding once the Venice Arsenal organized thousands of workers around standardized parts and specialized tasks?
candidates.notes: The Venice Arsenal used divided labor and standardized parts to mass-produce warships.

candidates.title: Rain Gauge
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became governable once a king could tax farmers based on measured rainfall reported from every village?
candidates.notes: A Korean king had rain gauges installed nationwide to help assess land taxes.

candidates.title: Coiled Spring
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for portable timekeeping once a coiled piece of metal could store and release energy?
candidates.notes: A coiled metal spring gave clockwork devices a compact way to store energy.

candidates.title: Arquebus
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for soldiers once a handheld firearm could be aimed and fired with both hands free?
candidates.notes: A pivoting match mechanism let soldiers aim and fire an early handheld gun.

candidates.title: Anemometer
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became measurable once a simple hinged plate could indicate the relative strength of the wind?
candidates.notes: A Renaissance polymath devised a simple hinged-plate instrument to gauge wind speed.

candidates.title: Printing Press with Movable Metal Type
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in the reach of ideas once a single press could produce hundreds of identical pages?
candidates.notes: Gutenberg's metal movable type let identical pages be printed by the hundreds.

candidates.title: Toothbrush
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for dental hygiene once a bristled brush replaced twigs and chewing sticks?
candidates.notes: Chinese boar-bristle brushes became the forerunner of the modern toothbrush.

candidates.title: Glass Mirror
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once mercury-backed glass could produce a far clearer reflection than polished metal?
candidates.notes: Venetian glassmakers backed glass with a tin-mercury amalgam for a clearer reflection.

candidates.title: Pocket Watch
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for the wealthy once time could be carried in a pocket rather than read from a public clock?
candidates.notes: Peter Henlein built the first portable, spring-driven pocket timepiece.

candidates.title: Etching for Print
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for printmakers once acid-etched lines let anyone who could draw produce a print, without engraving skill?
candidates.notes: Hopfer applied acid-etching techniques to printmaking, simplifying the process.

candidates.title: Sand Casting
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once a printed book made previously secret foundry techniques available to any reader?
candidates.notes: Biringuccio's printed book documented sand-casting and foundry techniques long kept secret.

candidates.title: Combination Lock
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for securing possessions once a lock could be opened by a memorized code rather than a physical key?
candidates.notes: Cardano devised a rotating-disc lock opened by a memorized combination.

candidates.title: Condom
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for sexual health once a barrier device was designed specifically to protect against the spread of syphilis?
candidates.notes: Falloppio devised a linen sheath meant to protect against syphilis.

candidates.title: Jointed Artificial Limb
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for wounded soldiers once surgeons abandoned cauterizing gunshot wounds with boiling oil in favor of gentler treatment and jointed prosthetics?
candidates.notes: Pare pioneered gentler wound treatment and jointed prosthetic limbs for amputees.

candidates.title: Graphite Pencil
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for writers once an erasable graphite mark could replace ink?
candidates.notes: A pure graphite deposit in England enabled the first erasable pencils.

candidates.title: Theodolite
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became surveyable once an instrument could measure both horizontal and vertical angles for triangulation?
candidates.notes: Digges's altazimuth instrument let surveyors triangulate land more precisely.

candidates.title: Gregorian Calendar
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened when Catholic, Protestant, and Orthodox countries disagreed for centuries over whether to accept a corrected calendar?
candidates.notes: Pope Gregory XIII's commission corrected calendar drift, but adoption split along religious lines for centuries.

candidates.title: Stocking Frame
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened when a monarch twice refused to patent a stocking-knitting machine out of concern for hand-knitters' livelihoods?
candidates.notes: William Lee's knitting machine was twice refused a royal patent to protect hand-knitters' jobs.

candidates.title: Microscope
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once a lens could reveal microorganisms and blood cells that no one had ever seen before?
candidates.notes: Combined lenses let van Leeuwenhoek become the first to observe microorganisms and blood cells.

candidates.title: Newspaper
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened when an early American newspaper was shut down by authorities after a single issue for publishing without official permission?
candidates.notes: Johann Carolus published the world's first printed newspaper, in Strasbourg.

candidates.title: Telescope
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in understanding of the cosmos once Galileo's telescope revealed sunspots, Jupiter's moons, and the phases of Venus?
candidates.notes: Lippershey's lens tube evolved into Galileo's telescope, revealing new features of the solar system.

candidates.title: Flintlock
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for soldiers once a spark-generating mechanism made firearms more reliable to load and fire?
candidates.notes: A French gunsmith's flintlock mechanism became a standard way to ignite gunpowder.

candidates.title: Cigarette
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed as tobacco spread from the Americas to Europe, and doctors' early praise for it gave way to bans and even executions for its use?
candidates.notes: Seville beggars rolled leftover cigar tobacco in paper to create the first cigarettes.

candidates.title: Slide Rule
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became calculable by hand once logarithmic scales let people multiply and divide without written arithmetic?
candidates.notes: Oughtred's sliding logarithmic scales became an early mechanical calculating device.

candidates.title: Mechanical Calculator
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for arithmetic once a mechanical device could add, subtract, multiply, and divide automatically?
candidates.notes: Schickard built an early mechanical 'calculating clock' that could perform basic arithmetic.

candidates.title: Vernier Scale
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became measurable to a finer degree once a sliding secondary scale let instruments read fractions of a division?
candidates.notes: Vernier's sliding scale let measuring instruments read to a finer precision.

candidates.title: Screw Micrometer
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became manufacturable to precise tolerances once a fine screw thread let workers measure minute distances?
candidates.notes: Gascoigne's spider-web-inspired marker let telescopes measure tiny angular distances precisely.

candidates.title: Barometer
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became forecastable once a column of mercury could reveal invisible changes in atmospheric pressure?
candidates.notes: Torricelli's mercury tube revealed and measured the pressure of the atmosphere.

candidates.title: Vacuum Pump
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became demonstrable about the natural world once a truly empty space could be created and studied?
candidates.notes: Guericke's vacuum pump let scientists create and study an artificial vacuum.

candidates.title: Pendulum Clock
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for timekeeping accuracy once a swinging pendulum, rather than a spring, regulated a clock?
candidates.notes: Huygens used a pendulum's steady swing to make clocks far more accurate.

candidates.title: Magic Lantern
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for popular entertainment once images could be projected large onto a wall using light and lenses?
candidates.notes: Huygens's lensed lantern let images be projected onto walls for audiences.

candidates.title: Hygrometer
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became measurable once a simple mechanical device could indicate the moisture content of the air?
candidates.notes: Folli built an early practical device for measuring air humidity.

candidates.title: Pressure Cooker
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for cooking once sealed, high-pressure steam could soften food and preserve nutrients faster than an open pot?
candidates.notes: Papin's 'steam digester' foreshadowed the modern pressure cooker.

candidates.title: Universal Joint
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became mechanically possible once a joint could transmit rotating power between shafts set at an angle to each other?
candidates.notes: Hooke's universal joint let rotating power 'go around corners' in machines.

candidates.title: Centrifugal Pump
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for mine safety once a rotating impeller could pump air or water more efficiently through tunnels?
candidates.notes: Papin's centrifugal pump helped ventilate mines and later powered furnaces.

candidates.title: Metronome
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for musicians once a mechanical device could mark a precise, adjustable tempo?
candidates.notes: Loulie's pendulum device gave musicians an early mechanical way to keep tempo.

candidates.title: Steam Pump
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for coal mining once steam power, rather than buckets, could drain flooded mine shafts?
candidates.notes: Savery's steam pump was an early attempt to drain floodwater from mines.

candidates.title: Seed Drill
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for farm yields once seeds could be sown evenly in rows instead of scattered by hand?
candidates.notes: Tull's horse-drawn seed drill increased crop yields up to eightfold.

candidates.title: Coke-based Iron Smelting
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for iron production and British industry once coke, rather than dwindling charcoal, could fuel bigger furnaces?
candidates.notes: Darby's coke-fired blast furnace let Britain produce iron cheaply and at scale.

candidates.title: Atmospheric Steam Engine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for mine drainage once atmospheric pressure and condensing steam could power a pump?
candidates.notes: Newcomen's engine used condensing steam to pump water out of mines.

candidates.title: Mercury Thermometer
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became comparable across places and people once temperature could be measured on a standardized, reproducible scale?
candidates.notes: Fahrenheit's mercury thermometer and fixed scale standardized temperature measurement.

candidates.title: Padlock
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for securing property once a lock's internal disks made it far more resistant to picking?
candidates.notes: Polhem's rotating-disk padlock resisted tampering better than earlier designs.

candidates.title: Pitot Tube
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became measurable about moving air and water once a simple tube could register flow speed from pressure differences?
candidates.notes: Pitot's tube measured flow rate and overturned assumptions about how water speed varies with depth.

candidates.title: Baby Carriage
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for childcare once a wheeled carriage, first built as an aristocratic toy, gained handles for pushing?
candidates.notes: Kent's shell-shaped carriage, first a children's amusement, evolved into the pushed baby carriage.

candidates.title: Flying Shuttle
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened when weavers saw a labor-saving loom device as a threat to their livelihoods?
candidates.notes: Kay's flying shuttle sped up weaving but was resisted by weavers who feared it would cost jobs.

candidates.title: Franklin Stove (Circulating Fireplace)
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for home heating safety once a more efficient stove design was deliberately left unpatented and freely shared?
candidates.notes: Franklin's more efficient, safer stove design was left unpatented to keep it freely available.

candidates.title: Leyden Jar
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became scientifically possible once electricity could be stored in a jar and discharged on demand?
candidates.notes: Van Musschenbroek's jar was the first device to store and discharge an electric charge.

candidates.title: Electroscope
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became detectable once a simple device could reveal and roughly measure invisible electric charge?
candidates.notes: Nollet's electroscope used repelling metal leaves to detect and measure electric charge.

candidates.title: Water Pillar Pump
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for mining once water pressure itself, rather than steam or muscle, could power the pumps draining a mine?
candidates.notes: Hell's water-powered pump helped drain deep mine shafts using hydraulic pressure.

candidates.title: Lightning Rod
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for buildings once lightning was proven to be electricity that could be safely channeled to the ground?
candidates.notes: Franklin's kite experiment led to the lightning rod, which protected buildings from fire.

candidates.title: Linnaean Taxonomy
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became organizable once every living thing could be classified within a single, shared naming system?
candidates.notes: Linnaeus's classification system organized all plant and animal life into a shared hierarchy.

candidates.title: Bimetallic Strip
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for temperature control once two bonded metals could bend predictably with heat?
candidates.notes: Harrison's bimetallic strip compensated for temperature changes in clock springs.

candidates.title: Marine Chronometer
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for maritime safety once a prize-winning clock let sailors calculate their longitude accurately at sea?
candidates.notes: Harrison's marine chronometer let ships determine their longitude and avoid getting lost at sea.

candidates.title: Spinning Jenny
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened when a machine that increased yarn output eightfold provoked spinners to break in and destroy it?
candidates.notes: Hargreaves's multi-spindle spinning jenny sharply increased yarn production but drew violent resistance.

candidates.title: Surveyor's Perambulator Wheel
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became mappable and divisible once land could be measured accurately with a simple rolling wheel?
candidates.notes: Fenn's perambulator wheel helped surveyors measure land for mapping and farm division.

candidates.title: Steam Engine with Separate Condenser
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for factories once Watt's more efficient steam engine could deliver rotary power beyond simple pumping?
candidates.notes: Watt's separate condenser made steam engines far more fuel-efficient and adaptable to factories.

candidates.title: Water Frame
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for cotton production once water power, rather than hand-cranking, could drive spinning machinery at factory scale?
candidates.notes: Arkwright's water-powered spinning frame led to the first true textile factory. candidates.title: Venetian Blind
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for homes once slatted blinds offered an adjustable alternative to heavy curtains?
candidates.notes: Slatted, tilting window blinds spread from Italy to become a popular curtain alternative.

candidates.title: Caterpillar Tracks
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for crossing rough terrain once continuous tracks, rather than wheels, could carry a vehicle's weight?
candidates.notes: Edgeworth's continuous-track design became the basis for later tracked vehicles.

candidates.title: Soda Water
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once carbon dioxide could be artificially infused into water to make it fizzy?
candidates.notes: Priestley created the first drinkable carbonated water, later commercialized as soda.

candidates.title: S-trap for Toilet
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for households once a water seal could keep sewer odors from entering the home?
candidates.notes: Cummings's S-shaped drain trap made it practical to bring the toilet indoors.

candidates.title: Submersible Craft
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for naval warfare once a single operator could pilot a vessel underwater to attack an enemy ship unseen?

candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What small everyday tasks changed once a stretchable rubber loop was available for fastening and bundling things?
candidates.notes: Perry finds a clever new use for rubber.

candidates.title: Pneumatic Tire
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did the earliest air-filled tire suggest about smoother travel, even though it went unadopted in its own time?
candidates.notes: Thomson’s cushion of air guarantees a smooth ride.

candidates.title: Rotary Printing Press
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about who could receive news, and how fast, once newspapers could be printed at far higher volumes and speeds?
candidates.notes: Hoe accelerates the printing process.

candidates.title: Hydraulic Crane
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for heavy lifting on docks and in industry once cranes could be driven by hydraulic power?
candidates.notes: Armstrong lifts weights using water power.

candidates.title: Printing Telegraph (Teleprinter)
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about telegraph messages once they could be printed automatically instead of read out letter by letter?
candidates.notes: House speeds written communication.

candidates.title: Chloroform Anesthetic
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about the experience and acceptance of pain in childbirth once chloroform offered doctors an alternative to ether?
candidates.notes: Simpson eases the pain of childbirth.

candidates.title: Chewing Gum
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about a small daily habit once a natural chewing resin could be sold commercially as gum?
candidates.notes: Curtis starts a masticatory fashion among North Americans.

candidates.title: Dry Cleaning
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about caring for delicate fabrics once clothes could be cleaned with solvent instead of water?
candidates.notes: Jolly discovers cleaning with solvents.

candidates.title: Francis Turbine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for power generation once water turbines could be engineered for far greater efficiency?
candidates.notes: Francis improves the water-driven turbine.

candidates.title: Safety Pin
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about a small daily need once a secure temporary fastener could be twisted from a single piece of wire?
candidates.notes: Hunt devises a perfect temporary fastener.

candidates.title: Oil Refinery
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What began to change in energy supply and industry once crude oil could be extracted and refined at commercial scale?
candidates.notes: Young extracts crude oil from coal.

candidates.title: Trawler Fishing
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about fish supply and the sea itself once nets could be dragged behind boats to catch indiscriminately?
candidates.notes: English fishermen devise a catch-all method.

candidates.title: Hydraulic Jack
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for heavy lifting once a compact device could exploit water pressure to move enormous loads?
candidates.notes: Dudgeon exploits water for heavy lifting.

candidates.title: Airship
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did the first steerable, passenger-carrying airship make thinkable about controlled flight decades before airplanes?
candidates.notes: Henri Giffard invents the first navigable full-sized airship.

candidates.title: Passenger Elevator
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for city buildings, and who was willing to ride to a high floor, once a safety brake made elevator travel trustworthy?
candidates.notes: Otis designs an elevator with a safety brake.

candidates.title: Rubber (Wellington) Boots
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about working outdoors in wet conditions once boots could be mass-produced from vulcanized rubber?
candidates.notes: Hutchinson produces waterproof boots.

candidates.title: Hypodermic Syringe
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about how medicine could be administered, and how precisely dosed, once drugs could be injected directly into the body rather than swallowed?
candidates.notes: Pravaz and Wood simultaneously develop a new means of administering medication.

candidates.title: Burglar Alarm
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about protecting property once a building's security could be monitored electrically rather than only by a night watchman?
candidates.notes: Augustus Pope patents a thief deterrent.

candidates.title: Prism Binoculars
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about viewing distant objects once binoculars could combine a wider field of view with real magnification?
candidates.notes: Porro makes distant things appear closer.

candidates.title: Bessemer Process
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible in construction, shipbuilding, and railways once steel could be mass-produced cheaply instead of made slowly in small batches?
candidates.notes: Bessemer provides cheap, plentiful steel for the Industrial Revolution.

candidates.title: Bunsen Burner
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about laboratory science once a clean, controllable flame could heat samples without excess soot or light?
candidates.notes: Bunsen improves a laboratory heat source.

candidates.title: Rotary Clothes Line
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about household chores once washing could be hung to dry on a space-saving rotary line?
candidates.notes: Higgins revolutionizes clothes hanging.

candidates.title: Celluloid
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once everyday objects could be molded from a synthetic material instead of made from scarce natural ones like ivory?
candidates.notes: Parkes fathers the plastics industry.

candidates.title: Mauveine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What began to change in fashion and industrial chemistry once vivid colors no longer depended on rare natural dyes?
candidates.notes: Perkin wins royal approval for his purple dye.

candidates.title: Military Camouflage
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about how armies were seen and organized once uniforms were designed to conceal soldiers rather than display them?
candidates.notes: The British Army sees the benefit of khaki.

candidates.title: Foghorn
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about guiding ships safely into harbor once fog warnings could be sounded by steam instead of bells or cannons?
candidates.notes: Foulis guides mariners into port using steam.

candidates.title: Tachistoscope
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about how much of the mind was understood to lie outside conscious awareness once experiments showed people responding to images they never consciously saw?
candidates.notes: Volkmann’s machine influences subconscious.

candidates.title: Rechargeable Storage Battery
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for portable and mobile power once a battery could be reliably recharged instead of discarded when spent?
candidates.notes: Planté invents the lead-acid ancestor of today’s car battery.

candidates.title: Spectrometer
