candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became knowable about the makeup of distant stars once their light could be analyzed rather than merely observed?
candidates.notes: Bunsen and Kirchhoff analyze light in terms of electromagnetic radiation.

candidates.title: Linoleum
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in the daily work of housekeeping once floors could be wiped clean instead of scrubbed or replaced?
candidates.notes: Walton turns a skin that formed on drying paint into a cheap, wipe-clean floor covering.

candidates.title: Gas-fired Engine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once an engine no longer needed a furnace and boiler to produce power?
candidates.notes: Lenoir builds the first gas-fired internal combustion engine as a compact alternative to the steam engine.

candidates.title: Repeating Rifle
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in warfare once one soldier could fire as fast as several using older muskets?
candidates.notes: Henry's lever-action repeating rifle lets one man deliver the firepower of several.

candidates.title: Color Photography
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once a photograph could reproduce the actual colors of a scene rather than only its shades of gray?
candidates.notes: Maxwell demonstrates the trichromatic process that becomes the foundation of all color photography.

candidates.title: Single-lens Reflex Camera
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for photographers once they could see through the lens exactly what the film would capture?
candidates.notes: Sutton patents the single-lens reflex design still used in modern cameras.

candidates.title: Twist Drill Bit
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible in construction and manufacturing once holes could be bored precisely instead of with an imprecise spade bit?
candidates.notes: Morse's helical twist drill replaces the crude, quickly dulled spade bit.

candidates.title: Solvay Process
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in industries like glassmaking and textiles once sodium carbonate could be produced cheaply and at scale?
candidates.notes: Solvay devises a more efficient, less polluting synthesis of sodium carbonate that eventually replaces the Leblanc process.

candidates.title: Yale Lock
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in how people secured property once a small, mass-producible cylinder lock replaced bulky ancient designs?
candidates.notes: Yale Jr. redesigns the ancient pin-tumbler lock into the compact, mass-producible cylinder lock still used today.

candidates.title: Snellen Eye Test
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became comparable and governable once vision itself could be reduced to a standardized fraction like 20/20?
candidates.notes: Snellen designs the letter chart that standardizes how visual acuity is measured and compared.

candidates.title: Machine Gun
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in the experience and scale of warfare once a single weapon could fire hundreds of rounds a minute?
candidates.notes: Gatling's crank-fired gun, later automated by Maxim, becomes the deadly, trench-defining weapon of industrial warfare.

candidates.title: Pasteurization
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in food safety once heat treatment could kill the bacteria responsible for spoilage and disease without ruining the product?
candidates.notes: Pasteur and Bernard show that heating milk kills bacteria that cause souring and disease, founding modern pasteurization.

candidates.title: Modern Harpoon
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened to whale populations, and eventually to the whaling industry itself, once steam boats and cannon-fired harpoons put previously unreachable whales within hunters' grasp?
candidates.notes: Foyn's steam-powered harpoon cannon opens up fast-swimming rorqual whales to hunting, making Norway the dominant whaling power.

candidates.title: Torpedo
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in naval warfare once ships could be attacked by an unmanned, self-propelled explosive rather than a manned assault?
candidates.notes: Luppis and Whitehead develop the self-propelled underwater torpedo, later sinking millions of tons of shipping in two world wars.

candidates.title: Barbed Wire
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed on the American frontier once land could be cheaply fenced, and who lost access to land that had previously been open?
candidates.notes: Jannin's wire fencing, cheaply mass-produced after Glidden's 1874 patent, lets settlers enclose land opened by the Homestead Act.

candidates.title: Roller Coaster
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in urban leisure once a mechanized ride could deliver a controlled thrill to paying crowds?
candidates.notes: Thompson's Switchback Railway at Coney Island launches the modern amusement-park roller coaster.

candidates.title: Ice-making Machine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What had to change in public trust before people would eat meat that had been mechanically refrigerated rather than freshly killed?
candidates.notes: Lowe's Compression Ice Machine pioneers mechanical refrigeration, though an early shipping venture failed partly on public skepticism about long-preserved meat.

candidates.title: Dry-cell Battery
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once batteries were safe and light enough to be used routinely in the home, in doorbells, cars, and telephones?
candidates.notes: Leclanché seals a lighter, less toxic battery design that becomes the basis of the modern dry cell.

candidates.title: Dynamite
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once explosive power once reserved for gunpowder became stable enough to mass produce, and how did its inventor reckon with being labeled a 'merchant of death'?
candidates.notes: Nobel stabilizes nitroglycerin into dynamite, starting the era of high explosives and later funding the Nobel Prizes.

candidates.title: Folding Ironing Board
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in the routine of home laundering once a dedicated, foldable board replaced tables and chairs?
candidates.notes: Mort designs a folding ironing board that can be stowed out of sight when not in use.

candidates.title: Antiseptic Surgery
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What had to change among surgeons, who had long worn a blood-soaked apron as a badge of expertise, before they would accept that invisible germs, not 'miasma,' caused wound infection?
candidates.notes: Lister applies carbolic acid to wounds and instruments based on Pasteur's germ theory, drastically cutting surgical gangrene despite ridicule from contemporaries.

candidates.title: Reinforced Concrete
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became structurally possible once concrete could be reinforced with metal to bear loads it could not bear alone?
candidates.notes: Monier's iron-and-concrete garden tubs establish the principle behind modern reinforced-concrete construction.

candidates.title: Paper Clip
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in office work once papers could be fastened and unfastened without pins or damage?
candidates.notes: Fay's wire fastener, originally meant for garment tags, becomes the ancestor of the paper clip.

candidates.title: Flat-bottomed Paper Bag
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did it take for a woman inventor's design to be recognized and protected, after a man stole her plans and a patent was initially granted to him instead?
candidates.notes: Margaret Knight designs a machine for flat-bottomed paper bags, fighting off a patent thief and initial dismissal from male colleagues before her invention spread worldwide.

candidates.title: Spring Tape Measure
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became easier to standardize and check once a flexible, retractable rule could measure curves as well as straight lines?
candidates.notes: Fellows patents a retractable spring tape measure nearly identical to those used today.

candidates.title: Stapler
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in binding documents once multiple staples could be loaded and driven in one motion rather than inserted by hand?
candidates.notes: Gould's wire stitcher is a direct predecessor of the modern paper stapler.

candidates.title: Margarine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened when a cheap butter substitute threatened dairy farmers' livelihoods, and how did they use licensing fees and color bans to slow its adoption?
candidates.notes: Mège-Mouriès invents oleomargarine as a cheap butter substitute, provoking a decades-long, government-backed backlash from the U.S. dairy industry.

candidates.title: Air Brake
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in rail safety once one driver could control every car's brakes instead of relying on brakemen scattered along the train?
candidates.notes: Westinghouse's air brake lets a single driver stop an entire train, dramatically improving rail safety.

candidates.title: Electrical Generator
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once a generator could produce smooth, high-voltage current reliably enough for industrial and later public use?
candidates.notes: Gramme's dynamo, and its later reversal into an electric motor, made electricity a genuinely practical industrial power source.

candidates.title: Cutting-wheel Can Opener
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in how households handled canned food once a can could be opened safely and easily rather than with a hammer and chisel?
candidates.notes: Lyman's rolling cutting wheel becomes the basis of the modern can opener.

candidates.title: Sandblasting
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What had to change in workplace safety once the health hazards of inhaled silica dust from sandblasting became apparent?
candidates.notes: Tilghman's sand-propelling process replaces expensive hand-chiseling for engraving and cleaning hard surfaces.

candidates.title: Compressed Air Rock Drill
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible in mining and tunneling once rock could be drilled mechanically instead of by hammer and brute force?
candidates.notes: Ingersoll's lightweight, tripod-mounted rock drill sharply increases the productivity of mining and tunnel-building.

candidates.title: Stock Ticker
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for investors once stock prices could reach them within minutes by wire instead of by runner or rumor?
candidates.notes: Edison's synchronized Universal Stock Ticker speeds the transmission of real-time stock prices to traders.

candidates.title: Automatic Lubrication
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did it mean for a Black inventor's work to become so trusted that people sought out 'the real McCoy' rather than the many imitations of his design?
candidates.notes: McCoy, son of escaped slaves, invents an automatic lubricating cup for locomotives, inspiring the phrase 'the real McCoy' amid a wave of imitators.

candidates.title: Vaseline ®
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did it take for people to trust and adopt a product marketed on the strength of a salesman deliberately burning and then healing his own skin?
candidates.notes: Chesebrough markets petroleum jelly as a healing product through dramatic self-demonstrations, despite it having no confirmed medicinal effect.

candidates.title: Cable Car
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became livable once a city's steep hills no longer limited where horse-drawn transport could reasonably go?
candidates.notes: Hallidie's cable car system lets San Francisco's hilly neighborhoods become practically accessible by public transit.

candidates.title: Modern DC Motor
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible in the home once electricity could be turned back into mechanical movement rather than only into light?
candidates.notes: Gramme shows that his dynamo design works in reverse, demonstrating the direct-current electric motor.

candidates.title: Blue Jeans
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for manual laborers once work trousers could survive rough use thanks to riveted pockets?
candidates.notes: Strauss and Davis patent rivet-reinforced denim work trousers that become the ancestor of blue jeans.

candidates.title: Automatic Fire Sprinkler
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in fire prevention once buildings could be defended automatically instead of relying on people noticing and fighting a fire, and why did insurers become the technology's biggest advocates?
candidates.notes: Parmelee's heat-triggered sprinkler head, adopted after insurance companies offered reduced premiums, launches the modern fire sprinkler.

candidates.title: Electric Tram
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about where people could afford to live once commuting to the center of a city became fast and cheap?
candidates.notes: Field's electric streetcar lets American city residents move out into new suburbs while still commuting quickly downtown.

candidates.title: Electric Dentist’s Drill
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in the experience of dental treatment once drills could spin fast enough to reduce pain and time in the chair?
candidates.notes: Green's electric drill sharply increases drilling speed over hand and pneumatic models, easing dental pain.

candidates.title: Firearm Magazine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for soldiers and hunters once a rifle could hold and feed multiple cartridges instead of requiring reloading after every shot?
candidates.notes: Hotchkiss designs a spring-loaded magazine system for bolt-action rifles, later mass-produced by Winchester.

candidates.title: Safety Razor
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about who shaved whom once a guarded blade made cutting yourself far less likely?
candidates.notes: The Kampfe brothers' guarded, removable-blade razor begins the shift of shaving from barbers to the individual at home.

candidates.title: Four-stroke Cycle
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for engines once a four-stroke cycle could reliably compress and ignite fuel rather than rely on earlier, less efficient designs?
candidates.notes: Otto's four-stroke internal combustion engine becomes the working model later adapted for motorcycles and automobiles.

candidates.title: Loudspeaker
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once electrical signals could be converted back into audible sound at a distance from their source?
candidates.notes: Bell patents the first electrical loudspeaker as part of his telephone system.

candidates.title: Telephone
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about who could reach whom, and how quickly, once speech itself—not just Morse code—could travel down a wire, despite a sitting U.S. president doubting anyone would want one?
candidates.notes: Bell's telephone lets actual speech travel by wire, and despite early skepticism, some 150,000 U.S. households had one within a decade.

candidates.title: Carpet Sweeper
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in home cleaning once carpets no longer had to be carried outside and beaten to remove dust?
candidates.notes: Bissell's rotating-bristle carpet sweeper offers an indoor alternative to beating rugs outdoors.

candidates.title: Microphone
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in the quality and reach of telephone conversation once the mouthpiece could amplify a voice rather than merely detect it?
candidates.notes: Berliner's loose-contact detector improves on Bell's weak telephone transmitter and earns him a role at Bell's company.

candidates.title: Phonograph
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about memory and time once a voice or sound, not just an image, could be captured and replayed at will?
candidates.notes: Edison's phonograph is the first device able to record and replay sound, letting a moment of speech or music outlive the moment itself.

candidates.title: Milk/Cream Separator
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in dairy production once cream could be separated from milk by centrifugal force in minutes rather than by gravity over a day?
candidates.notes: Laval's centrifugal separator speeds cream extraction and reduces waste compared to letting milk settle.

candidates.title: Time Zones
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What had to be agreed upon, and by whom, before towns that had each kept their own local time could be coordinated across a continent by rail schedule?
candidates.notes: Fleming's proposal for worldwide 15-degree time zones, prompted by railway scheduling chaos, is adopted globally at the 1884 International Meridian Conference.

candidates.title: Cathode Ray Tube
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in physicists' understanding of matter once the glow inside a vacuum tube turned out to be a stream of something material, not just light?
candidates.notes: Crookes's vacuum tube experiments on 'radiant matter' set the stage for the later discovery of the electron.

candidates.title: Rebreather
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible underwater once a diver could recycle exhaled air instead of needing a constant fresh supply?
candidates.notes: Fleuss builds the first scuba rebreather, recycling breathable gas via a carbon dioxide scrubber.

candidates.title: Cash Register
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in the relationship between employers and employees once every sale could be automatically recorded rather than trusted to a clerk's honesty?
candidates.notes: Ritty invents the cash register specifically to stop his saloon staff from pocketing the takings.

candidates.title: Medical Autoclave
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in surgery once instruments could be sterilized at temperatures high enough to kill all known bacteria?
candidates.notes: Chamberland's pressurized steam autoclave, built to help prove Pasteur's germ theory, becomes standard for sterilizing surgical tools.

candidates.title: Saccharin
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did it take for a substance discovered by accident on unwashed hands to become both a trusted household product and a decades-long subject of safety controversy and political intervention?
candidates.notes: Remsen and Fahlberg discover saccharin by accident, and its safety is debated and politically contested for over a century.

candidates.title: Seismograph
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became knowable about the Earth's interior once instruments could continuously record movements invisible and imperceptible to people on the surface?
candidates.notes: Milne's horizontal pendulum seismograph enables continuous recording of earthquakes and, later, discoveries about Earth's internal structure.

candidates.title: Spring-loaded Mousetrap
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in pest control once a simple mechanical trap could kill a rodent instantly and repeatedly without human presence?
candidates.notes: Maxim's spring-loaded trap, invented as a teenager, establishes the classic mousetrap design still used today.

candidates.title: Cholera Vaccine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in disease prevention once an artificially weakened, lab-grown culture—rather than a naturally occurring one—could reliably produce immunity?
candidates.notes: Pasteur discovers, partly by accident with spoiled chicken cultures, that an artificial weakened bacteria culture can vaccinate against cholera.

candidates.title: Incubator
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for premature infants, once placed in jars of feathers to keep warm, once a simple heated chamber could support their survival?
candidates.notes: Tarnier and Martin adapt a poultry incubator design into a device that helps save premature babies, transforming odds that were once left to jars of feathers.

candidates.title: Ballcock
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became automatic in plumbing once a floating valve could regulate water flow without anyone watching the cistern fill?
candidates.notes: Crapper's ballcock float valve automatically stops a toilet cistern from overflowing.

candidates.title: Free-jet Water Turbine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for mining operations once falling water could be converted into power more efficiently than any earlier waterwheel?
candidates.notes: Pelton's split-cup water turbine design becomes far more efficient than earlier waterwheels used to power mines.

candidates.title: Metal Detector
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did the limits of a hastily built device reveal, when it failed to find a bullet inside a dying U.S. president because of an unusual metal bed frame nobody accounted for?
candidates.notes: Bell rushes to build a metal detector to find the bullet lodged in assassinated President Garfield, but an unnoticed metal bed frame defeats it.

candidates.title: Septic Tank
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for households without access to a main sewer line once waste could be broken down and drained safely on-site?
candidates.notes: Mouras's septic tank lets waste decompose and drain without connection to a municipal sewer system.

candidates.title: Halftone Engraving
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in newspapers and books once photographs, not just text and line drawings, could be printed at scale?
candidates.notes: Ives's halftone process converts continuous-tone photographs into printable dot patterns still used in newspapers today.

candidates.title: Revolving Door
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about entering and leaving a building once a rotating door could control both foot traffic and the loss of heated or cooled air?
candidates.notes: Bockhacker's revolving door design reduces collisions at entrances and later proves to save significant amounts of energy.

candidates.title: Blowtorch
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for small-scale soldering, cooking, and repair work once intense, directed heat could come from a compact handheld tool?
candidates.notes: Nyberg's blowtorch, a byproduct of his failed flying-machine experiments, becomes a widely used handheld heat tool.

candidates.title: Electric Iron
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in the drudgery of ironing once a hot plate could be heated by electricity instead of by a coal stove?
candidates.notes: Seely patents the first electric iron, eventually replacing coal- and kerosene-heated flat irons in most homes.

candidates.title: Cantilever Bridge
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What had to be rebuilt, in engineering confidence as much as steel, after an earlier bridge across the same waterway had collapsed and killed seventy-five people?
candidates.notes: Baker and Fowler's steel cantilever Forth Rail Bridge replaces a design by the engineer whose earlier Tay Bridge had collapsed fatally.

candidates.title: Public Electricity Supply
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in daily urban life once electric light and power could be centrally generated and distributed to many buildings at once, rather than produced individually?
candidates.notes: Edison's Pearl Street Station delivers the first permanent, centralized commercial electricity supply, beginning the shift away from gaslight.

candidates.title: Electric Fan
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about who could afford relief from summer heat once desktop fans went from a luxury for the rich to a mass-produced household item?
candidates.notes: Wheeler's brass desktop fan becomes affordable to ordinary households only once steel blades could be mass-produced in the 1920s.

candidates.title: Induction Motor
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in industrial and household machinery once a motor using alternating current could be built more simply and cheaply than direct-current designs?
candidates.notes: Tesla's induction motor, running on alternating current, becomes the basis for most modern household appliances.

candidates.title: Image Rasterization
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became conceivable in transmitting images once a picture could be broken into a rapid sequence of light and dark signals?
candidates.notes: Nipkow's spinning disk converts images into electrical signals, laying the technical groundwork for television.

candidates.title: Punchcard Accounting
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became governable about a population once its census data could be sorted and tabulated by machine instead of by hand?
candidates.notes: Hollerith's punchcard tabulator cuts census processing time by more than half, saving millions and eventually giving rise to IBM.

candidates.title: Linotype Machine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened to the labor and cost of publishing once a keyboard-operated machine could cast whole lines of type, replacing letter-by-letter handsetting?
candidates.notes: Mergenthaler's Linotype machine mechanizes typesetting, reducing skilled labor needs and fueling a boom in newspaper and magazine publishing.

candidates.title: Portable Automatic Machine Gun
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in the scale of casualties once a machine gun's own recoil could keep it firing automatically as long as the trigger was held?
candidates.notes: Maxim's fully automatic, water-cooled machine gun becomes the prototype for the weapon that dominates trench warfare.

candidates.title: Kraft Process
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for the paper industry once wood pulp, not just rags, could be turned into strong paper at scale?
candidates.notes: Dahl's kraft process produces stronger wood-pulp paper and eventually overtakes the earlier sulphite process.

candidates.title: Dissolvable Pill
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in taking medicine once a pill could reliably dissolve in the stomach instead of passing through the body intact or requiring liquid dosing?
candidates.notes: Upjohn's layered, easily crushable pill dissolves reliably, replacing inconsistent liquid doses and hard-coated pills.

candidates.title: Franking Machine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in the business of mail once postage could be printed and metered by machine instead of relying on a signature-based privilege open to abuse?
candidates.notes: Bushe conceives a machine to print postage and meter its cost, addressing the time cost of stamping mail by hand.

candidates.title: Steel-girder Skyscraper
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for cities with limited ground space once a steel skeleton, not load-bearing walls, could carry a building's weight?
candidates.notes: Jenney's steel-framed Home Insurance Building in Chicago establishes the structural principle behind the modern skyscraper.

candidates.title: Steam Turbine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible in power generation and marine propulsion once steam's energy could be harnessed through staged turbine blades instead of pistons?
candidates.notes: Parsons's staged steam turbine dramatically outperforms older piston engines and is soon used in power stations and warships.

candidates.title: Photovoltaic (Solar) Cell
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did it mean to build a technology decades before it could be efficient enough to be useful at any scale?
candidates.notes: Fritts builds the first solar cell from selenium and gold, though at only 1 percent efficiency it remains a curiosity for decades.

candidates.title: Gas Mantle
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in street and home lighting once gas flames could produce a brighter, whiter light without extra smoke and smell?
candidates.notes: Welsbach's thorium-based mantle improves gas lighting shortly before electric lighting displaces it.

candidates.title: Electric Arc Welding
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible in joining metal once an electric arc, not just a flame, could generate enough heat to fuse two pieces together?
candidates.notes: Benardos and Olszewski patent an electrode holder that establishes the basis of electric arc welding.

candidates.title: Modern Safety Bicycle
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about who could safely ride a bicycle once equal-sized wheels replaced the dangerously tall penny-farthing?
candidates.notes: Starley's Rover Safety bicycle, with its low, balanced frame and chain drive, makes cycling more widespread and affordable.

candidates.title: Motorcycle
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in personal transport once a gas engine could be strapped to a bicycle frame, however unstable the result?
candidates.notes: Daimler and Maybach fit a gas engine to a strengthened bicycle, creating what historians regard as the first motorcycle.

candidates.title: Rabies Vaccine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in the treatment of a once-certain death sentence once a graduated series of injections could be administered after exposure, not just before?
candidates.notes: Pasteur's dried-spinal-cord rabies vaccine, first tested on a bitten boy in 1885, proves effective even given after infection.

candidates.title: Transformer
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible in delivering electricity over distance once voltage could be raised for transmission and safely lowered again for use?
candidates.notes: Stanley's transformer lets alternating current be converted between voltages, minimizing energy loss over distance.

candidates.title: Supercharger
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for engine performance once extra air could be forced into a cylinder rather than relying on atmospheric pressure alone?
candidates.notes: Daimler's twin-rotor supercharger boosts engine power, later becoming essential to racing cars and wartime aircraft.

candidates.title: Hall-Héroult Process
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once a metal once so precious it capped the Washington Monument could suddenly be produced cheaply and in bulk?
candidates.notes: Hall and Héroult's electrolytic process turns aluminum from a rare, painstakingly produced metal into an everyday material.

candidates.title: Dishwasher
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in domestic and hospitality labor once dishes could be cleaned by machine under pressurized water rather than by hand?
candidates.notes: Cochrane, tired of servants chipping her china, designs a dishwasher that eventually becomes standard in Western kitchens.

candidates.title: Motorcar
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about daily distance, urban form, and even mortality once a self-propelled car, not a horse, could carry people wherever roads allowed—and what convinced a skeptical public it was reliable?
candidates.notes: Benz's patented motorcar, proven reliable by his wife Bertha's unassisted 60-mile publicity drive, launches an automobile age later tied to tens of millions of deaths, climate change, and suburban sprawl.

candidates.title: Contact Lenses
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did people tolerate—pain, swelling, brief wearing times—before contact lens materials advanced enough to be worn comfortably?
candidates.notes: Fick, Kalt, and Müller independently invent glass contact lenses, though they cause discomfort until plastics improve them decades later.

candidates.title: Monotype Machine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible in correcting and refining printed text once individual letters, not whole cast lines, could be set and adjusted by machine?
candidates.notes: Lanston's Monotype system casts individual letters from punched paper tape, allowing finer control than the competing Linotype machine.

candidates.title: Motorboat
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did it take to convince nervous early buyers that a petrol engine was safe enough to trust on the water?
candidates.notes: Daimler and Maybach's motorboat, its engine deceptively described as 'oil-electrical' to ease buyer fears, becomes an early commercial success.

candidates.title: Phonograph Record
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in recorded sound once a flat, easily manufactured disc could replace the cumbersome wax cylinder?
candidates.notes: Berliner's flat phonograph disc, played with a horizontally moving stylus, becomes easier to manufacture than earlier cylinders.

candidates.title: Ballpoint Pen
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What kept a promising writing tool from being adopted for half a century, until its core flaw—uncontrollable ink flow—was finally solved?
candidates.notes: Loud patents the first ballpoint pen, but leaking and clogging keep it out of commercial use until Bíró's improvements decades later.

candidates.title: Deodorant
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in the everyday management of the body once a trademarked product, not homemade remedies, promised to control body odor?
candidates.notes: An unnamed Philadelphia inventor markets 'Mum,' the first trademarked deodorant, using zinc chloride to inhibit odor-causing bacteria.

candidates.title: Vending Machine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in retail once a product could be sold without a person present to hand it over?
candidates.notes: Adams's coin-operated chewing gum machine popularizes automated selling, later extended to countless other goods.

candidates.title: Dictating Machine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did stenographers stand to lose, and how did they resist, once a machine offered to record dictation without a human transcriber?
candidates.notes: Edison's improved phonograph-based dictating machine meets fierce early opposition from stenographers worried about their jobs.

candidates.title: AC Electric Power
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did it take to convince the public and industry to adopt alternating current once Edison waged a propaganda campaign to brand it as dangerous?
candidates.notes: Tesla's AC power system, championed by Westinghouse against Edison's DC system and smear campaign, eventually becomes the world's dominant form of electricity.

candidates.title: Electricity Meter
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became commercially possible once the amount of alternating current a household used could be measured and billed, not just estimated by the lamp?
candidates.notes: Shallenberger's AC electricity meter, discovered from a spring's odd movement, lets Westinghouse charge customers for the power he supplied.

candidates.title: Kinematograph
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What was lost to history when an early moving-picture inventor vanished just before he could publicly claim credit for his work?
candidates.notes: Le Prince patents an early moving-image camera and films the first known motion picture, then disappears before he can reveal it publicly.

candidates.title: Electric Speedometer
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became knowable to a driver, in real time, once a car's speed could be shown on a dial rather than only estimated from distance and time?
candidates.notes: Belusic patents an early electric velocimeter, a forerunner of the modern automobile speedometer.

candidates.title: Wind Turbine Generator
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for a rural estate or village once wind, not just water or coal, could be converted directly into electric light?
candidates.notes: Brush links a wind-powered rotor to a generator to light his own estate, an early forerunner of the modern wind turbine.

candidates.title: Brassiere
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for women's bodies and daily comfort once a divided garment could replace the whalebone corset, and why did wartime necessity finally make it commonplace?
candidates.notes: Cadolle splits the corset into a supportive upper garment using elastic, but the bra only becomes widespread once World War I metal shortages push women out of corsets and into factory work.

candidates.title: Electric Drill
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible in mining, construction, and eventually home repair once a drill could be powered by electricity rather than by hand or bow?
candidates.notes: Arnot's electric drill, first built for mining, becomes the ancestor of the modern power tool and home-improvement culture.

candidates.title: Jukebox
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in shared public listening once recorded music, not a live player piano, could be summoned by anyone with a coin?
candidates.notes: Glass's coin-operated 'nickel-in-the-slot phonograph' displaces the player piano as the dominant way groups hear music in public.

candidates.title: Clutch
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for drivers once an engine could be disengaged from the wheels smoothly instead of stalling at every stop?
candidates.notes: Daimler and Maybach's friction clutch lets a car's engine and wheels separate for smoother starts and gear changes.

candidates.title: Motorcar Gears
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for early drivers once a car could shift between gears to stay efficient at different speeds, rather than run at one fixed ratio?
candidates.notes: Benz adds a second gear and gear shift to his motorcar, an idea reportedly suggested by his wife Bertha after her long-distance drive.

candidates.title: Two-Stroke Engine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What trade-off did users accept—more pollution for less weight—when choosing a two-stroke engine over a four-stroke one?
candidates.notes: Day's simplified two-stroke engine becomes popular in motorbikes and small equipment despite being more polluting than four-stroke designs.

candidates.title: Photographic Film
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about who could be a photographer once a simple box camera, preloaded with flexible film, replaced fragile glass plates and specialist skill?
candidates.notes: Eastman's roll film and Kodak box camera let ordinary people take photographs for the first time, wresting photography away from professionals and the elite.

candidates.title: Payphone
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in access to communication once anyone passing by, not just telephone owners, could make a call for a coin?
candidates.notes: Gray's coin-operated payphone spreads telephone access to travelers and the public, fueling demand for home telephones too.

candidates.title: Accelerator/Throttle
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for drivers once engine power, and therefore speed, could be controlled by a single mechanism rather than fixed settings?
candidates.notes: Benz's accelerator/throttle lets drivers control an engine's fuel-air mixture and thus a car's speed.

candidates.title: Coherer
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became detectable, and therefore usable for communication, once invisible electromagnetic waves could trigger a measurable change in a simple tube of metal filings?
candidates.notes: Branly's coherer detects Hertzian (radio) waves, becoming the basis for wireless telegraphy.

candidates.title: Automatic Telephone Exchange
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in trust and privacy once calls could be automatically routed by number, after a human operator had been quietly diverting a competitor's business calls?
candidates.notes: Strowger, suspecting a rival's wife of diverting his calls as the local exchange operator, invents an automatic exchange that removes the human intermediary.

candidates.title: Blow-dry Hair Dryer
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in hair styling once heat, not just brushing, could be used to control shape at a salon?
candidates.notes: Godefroy's makeshift bonnet-and-chimney dryer introduces blow-drying to hair salons.

candidates.title: Lawn Sprinkler
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for suburban homeowners once piped city water and a rotating sprinkler let anyone irrigate a lawn or garden?
candidates.notes: Oswald's rotating sprinkler improves on earlier static designs as suburban gardening spreads alongside city water systems.

candidates.title: Spark Ignition
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became reliable about the internal combustion engine once a spark, precisely timed, could ignite fuel rather than relying on a pilot flame?
candidates.notes: Benz's spark ignition system helps make the gasoline-fueled internal combustion engine practical and reliable.

candidates.title: Electric Chair
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did it mean for the state to adopt a mode of execution that was, in part, a weapon in a corporate rivalry over whose electrical current the public should trust?
candidates.notes: Edison and Brown push alternating current for the electric chair partly to brand AC as dangerous in their commercial rivalry with Westinghouse, making Kemler's 1890 execution the first electrocution.

candidates.title: Pneumatic Hammer
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible on construction and shipbuilding sites once a percussive tool could be driven by compressed air instead of a worker's arm alone?
candidates.notes: King's compressed-air pneumatic hammer boosts worker productivity in construction, shipbuilding, and mining at a moment of rapid industrial growth.

candidates.title: Frasch Process
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became extractable, and where, once superheated water and compressed air could melt and lift sulfur from deep underground rather than requiring shallow mining?
candidates.notes: Frasch's process for melting and pumping deep sulfur deposits eventually helps the U.S. become self-sufficient in sulfur production.

candidates.title: Carborundum
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for precision manufacturing once a synthetic abrasive nearly as hard as diamond could be produced in a factory?
candidates.notes: Acheson accidentally creates silicon carbide while trying to synthesize diamonds, yielding an industrially vital abrasive.

candidates.title: Electric Car Battery
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened to an early, viable transportation technology once gasoline-powered cars proved cheaper and more practical, and what does its near-disappearance say about how societies choose between competing technologies?
candidates.notes: Morrison's storage battery powers one of the first successful electric cars, a technology that nearly vanished by the 1930s in favor of gasoline vehicles.

candidates.title: Dow Process
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did a small American company have to do to compete against an established European cartel that tried to flood the market and undercut a new domestic producer?
candidates.notes: Dow's electrolytic bromine extraction process lets him compete against and eventually be invited into the German-led Bromkonvention cartel.

candidates.title: Kinetoscope
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible in entertainment once individual viewers, not audiences, could peer into a box and watch moving images on demand?
candidates.notes: Edison and Dickson's peep-hole Kinetoscope, showing perforated celluloid film, helps launch the motion picture industry.

candidates.title: Wireless Communication
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Who received credit and financial reward for inventing radio, and what did it take decades later for the patent record to be corrected?
candidates.notes: Tesla develops practical radio technology and patents, but Marconi wins public fame and money until the U.S. Patent Office overturns his patent in Tesla's favor after Tesla's death.

candidates.title: Escalator
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in moving people through department stores, transit stations, and stadiums once stairs could carry passengers automatically?
candidates.notes: Reno's 'inclined elevator,' first built as a Coney Island amusement, becomes the ancestor of the modern escalator.

candidates.title: Swiss Army Knife
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for soldiers once a single tool could combine a blade, screwdriver, can opener, and punch that they had previously needed several separate tools to carry?
candidates.notes: Elsener creates a multifunctional pocket knife for the Swiss army after learning its knives had been made in Germany.

candidates.title: Adjustable Wrench
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became easier for mechanics once one adjustable tool could fit many differently sized nuts and bolts, at a time when no standard sizing existed?
candidates.notes: Johansson's adjustable wrench replaces the need to carry a separate tool for every unstandardized nut and bolt size.

candidates.title: Thermal Cracking of Oil
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became usable as fuel once heavy crude oil molecules could be broken into lighter ones by heat and pressure?
candidates.notes: Shukhov's thermal cracking process converts more of each barrel of crude oil into usable fuels like gasoline and kerosene.

candidates.title: Tire Valve
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became practical about the pneumatic tire once it could be reliably inflated and sealed through a small, dependable valve?
candidates.notes: Schrader's tire valve design becomes a nearly unchanged industry standard for over a century.

candidates.title: Crown Bottle Cap
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in the bottling industry once a cheap, gripping metal cap could reliably seal in carbonation, and what convinced brewers to retool for it?
candidates.notes: Painter's Crown Cork, proven by shipping sealed beer successfully to South America, comes to supply nearly half the world's bottle caps by the 1930s.

candidates.title: Fingerprinting
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed when police forces could match a suspect to a crime through fingerprints instead of relying on eyewitnesses or body measurements?
candidates.notes: Vucetich adds a key component to forensics.

candidates.title: Vacuum Flask
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once liquids could be reliably kept hot or cold outside a laboratory?
candidates.notes: Dewar invents the forerunner to Thermos.

candidates.title: Duplex Telegraph
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once a single telegraph wire could carry messages in both directions at once?
candidates.notes: Edison speeds up telegraph communication.

candidates.title: Electric Arc Furnace
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for industry once electric arcs could reach temperatures ordinary furnaces could not?
candidates.notes: Moissan aids the production of chemicals.

candidates.title: Ferris Wheel
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed when a single structure could lift thousands of fairgoers at once for a view of an entire city?
candidates.notes: Ferris creates an engineering wonder to put Chicago on the entertainment map.

candidates.title: Carburetor
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for engine design once fuel and air could be mixed in a controlled, steady spray?
candidates.notes: Bánki and Csonka fuel the newly invented motor car.

candidates.title: Milking Machine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for dairy farming once milking could be mechanized without routinely injuring the cow?
candidates.notes: The Thistle company devises a high-yielding, safer machine.

candidates.title: Breakfast Cereal
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened when a food invented for a strict health regimen was reshaped with added sugar to sell commercially, over one of its inventors' objections?
candidates.notes: The Kelloggs invent a popular breakfast food.

candidates.title: Breast Implant
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Who bore the risk while surgeons experimented for decades with wax, ivory, glass, and fat transplants before safer breast implant materials were found?
candidates.notes: Czerny introduces plastic surgery.

candidates.title: Diesel Engine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for industry once an engine could ignite fuel from compression alone, without a spark?
candidates.notes: Diesel patents a fuel-economic engine.

candidates.title: Film Camera/Projector
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed when moving pictures could be projected for many people at once instead of viewed one person at a time?
candidates.notes: The Lumière brothers popularize movies.

candidates.title: X-ray Photography
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed when doctors could see inside a living body before anyone understood that the rays doing the seeing could also cause cancer?
candidates.notes: Röntgen discovers how to photograph inside the bodies of living things.

candidates.title: Liquefaction of Air
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for industry and medicine once gases could be liquefied and produced in bulk?
candidates.notes: Von Linde founds modern refrigeration.

candidates.title: Electric Stove
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What limited early adoption of the electric stove, and who could actually use one before household electricity was common?
candidates.notes: Hadaway patents a new cooking device.

candidates.title: Magnetic Recording
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible once sound could be captured as a pattern of magnetism rather than a physical groove?
candidates.notes: Poulsen’s invention achieves the first magnetic audio recording.

candidates.title: Powered Hearing Aid
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for people with hearing loss once amplification no longer depended on a passive horn or trumpet?
candidates.notes: Hutchinson’s invention lends power to the hard of hearing.

candidates.title: Heroin
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Who had to adjust once a drug marketed by a major pharmaceutical company as a cure for morphine addiction turned out to be addictive itself, leading to its criminalization?
candidates.notes: Hoffmann develops a drug initially thought suitable to replace morphine.

candidates.title: Portable Electric Flashlight
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for ordinary people once portable light no longer required an open flame?
candidates.notes: Misell and Hubert provide handheld light.

candidates.title: Steering Wheel
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for drivers once a rotating wheel replaced the steering tiller, and who lost out in the ensuing patent race?
candidates.notes: Winton’s system gives drivers more control.

candidates.title: Self-heating Food Can
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for travelers once food could be heated by its own chemical reaction rather than an external flame?
candidates.notes: Unknown inventor makes hot food on the go possible.

candidates.title: Aspirin
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did it mean for medicine that a drug used successfully by millions for decades had its actual mechanism of action discovered only in 1971?
candidates.notes: Hoffman invents one of the most popular painkillers of all time.

candidates.title: Band Brake
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for automobile safety once braking no longer depended on a wooden block pressed against a tire?
candidates.notes: Daimler makes driving more secure.

candidates.title: Assembly Line
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in how goods were produced once a single company reorganized its workers into a sequential assembly line, a system other manufacturers then copied and refined?
candidates.notes: Olds invents a revolutionary system for industry.

candidates.title: Meccano
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for children's play once a single reusable kit of parts could be built into almost anything and then rebuilt?
candidates.notes: Hornby invents a classic and much-loved construction toy.

candidates.title: Radiotherapy
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Who bore the risk while doctors used radiation on tumors before anyone could measure or control the dose, and how did that change once radiation units were defined?
candidates.notes: Scientists put radiation to positive use as a treatment for cancer.

candidates.title: Disposable Razor Blade
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in men's daily grooming once a blade could simply be replaced instead of sharpened?
candidates.notes: Gillette revolutionizes men’s personal hygiene.

candidates.title: Portable “Brownie” Camera
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about who got to take photographs once a camera was cheap and simple enough for a child to use?
candidates.notes: Brownell and Kodak develop a camera for use by everybody.

candidates.title: Instant Coffee
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for coffee drinkers once brewing could be replaced by dissolving a powder in hot water?
candidates.notes: Kato invents the quick caffeine fix.

candidates.title: Flame Thrower
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did it mean for soldiers and civilians once a weapon designed to spread fire became, in the book's words, the most demoralizing infantry weapon ever used, while remaining dangerous to the people who carried it?
candidates.notes: Fiedler conceives a devastating weapon.

candidates.title: Toy Electric Train Set
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for toy manufacturing once a model train could run on electricity without supervision?
candidates.notes: Cowen invents a timeless toy for young and old.

candidates.title: Improved Radio Transmitter
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for radio once a transmitter could carry a continuous wave capable of carrying a human voice, not just a telegraph pulse?
candidates.notes: Fessenden sends the first audio radio transmission.

candidates.title: Mercury Vapor Lamp
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for lighting once a gas discharge tube could be made to glow steadily, decades before it was refined into fluorescent light?
candidates.notes: Hewitt pioneers fluorescent lighting.

candidates.title: Electric Vacuum Cleaner
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for households once dust could be sucked away rather than simply blown into the air?
candidates.notes: Booth’s machine makes light of housework.

candidates.title: Zoom Lens
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for photographers once a single lens could change its focal length instead of requiring the photographer to physically move?
candidates.notes: Allen brings a sharper focus to photography.

candidates.title: Laparoscope
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for surgical patients once a surgeon could look inside the abdomen and eventually operate through a tiny incision instead of a large open one?
candidates.notes: Kelling revolutionizes abdominal surgery.

candidates.title: Gun Silencer
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for shooters once a firearm could be discharged without the traditional loud report?
candidates.notes: Maxim silences his father’s invention, the Maxim gun.

candidates.title: Air Conditioning
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about where and when people could live and work once indoor air could be mechanically cooled, given the book's claim that it could cut heat-related deaths by up to 40 percent?
candidates.notes: Carrier makes the world a much cooler place to live.

candidates.title: Drum Brake
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for drivers once braking relied on friction pads pressing against a rotating drum rather than a wooden block?
candidates.notes: Renault uses friction to slow down motor cars.

candidates.title: Disk Brake
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Why did manufacturers keep choosing the cheaper, less responsive drum brake over the disk brake for nearly fifty years after the better design existed?
candidates.notes: Lanchester introduces a modern car braking system ahead of its time.

candidates.title: Ostwald Process
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did it mean for a war's outcome that a chemical process for manufacturing nitric acid let a nation keep making explosives after its natural supply of nitrate was cut off?
candidates.notes: Ostwald manufactures nitric acid.

candidates.title: Teddy Bear
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in children's culture once a newspaper cartoon about a president's mercy toward a bear turned into a mass-produced toy?
candidates.notes: Iconic children’s toy is named after Roosevelt.

candidates.title: Spark Plug
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for automobile engines once ignition no longer risked draining the battery or setting the engine on fire?
candidates.notes: Honold paves the way for engines with higher operating speeds.

candidates.title: Electrocardiograph
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for diagnosing heart disease once the heart's own electrical activity could be recorded on paper?
candidates.notes: Einthoven’s machine provides a major boost to diagnosing heart problems.

candidates.title: Blink Comparator
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for astronomers once two photographs of the same sky could be flicked between to reveal anything that had moved or changed?
candidates.notes: Pulfrich’s apparatus improves observation of the skies.

candidates.title: Arc Transmitter
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for wireless communication once a transmitter could generate a continuous radio wave instead of a series of fading sparks?
candidates.notes: Poulsen creates a portable radio system.

candidates.title: Crayons
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for children's art once a safe, nontoxic wax coloring stick was made specifically for them?
candidates.notes: Binney and Smith bring out the artist in kids.

candidates.title: Wire Coat Hanger
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in retail display once a simple bent-wire hanger could be mass produced cheaply?
candidates.notes: Parkhouse’s idea keeps clothes crease-free.

candidates.title: Windshield Wiper
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Who had to adjust once a device patented in 1903 to keep a windshield clear went unwanted for over a decade until cars became common enough for anyone to want one?
candidates.notes: Anderson gives drivers a clear view.

candidates.title: Glass Bottle-making Machine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for child laborers once a fully automatic glass bottle-making machine did the work that had previously employed children as cheap glassblowing labor?
candidates.notes: Owens invention does more to eliminate child labor than previous legislative efforts.

candidates.title: Powered Airplane
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What had to be worked out through years of glider testing before sustained, controlled, powered flight became possible?
candidates.notes: The Wright brothers build the first winged aircraft capable of sustained flight.

candidates.title: Tea Bag
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Why did it take British tea-drinkers decades longer than Americans to accept the tea bag, and what does that delay suggest about resistance to a convenience product?
candidates.notes: Sullivan accidentally discovers a way to brew an instant cup of tea.

candidates.title: Automatic Transmission
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for driving once gears could shift without the driver disengaging a clutch?
candidates.notes: Sturtevant renders gear sticks superfluous.

candidates.title: Answering Machine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about people's control over being reachable by phone once a missed call could be recorded rather than simply lost?
candidates.notes: Poulsen develops a solution for missed phone calls.

candidates.title: Valve Diode
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for early electronics once current could be made to flow in one direction only, inside a sealed vacuum?
candidates.notes: Fleming invents the first true electronic device.

candidates.title: Tractor
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for farm work once a tracked vehicle no longer sank into soft soil the way wheeled traction engines had?
candidates.notes: Holt invents caterpillar tracks.

candidates.title: Derailleur Gears
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did it take to convince skeptical cyclists to accept variable gears, given that the inventor had to stage a race between a single-speed and a derailleur bike just to win them over?
candidates.notes: De Vivie makes cycling easier.

candidates.title: Turbocharger
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for engine efficiency once exhaust gases, instead of being wasted, could be used to force more air into the cylinders?
candidates.notes: Büchi reclaims lost energy to make engines more efficient.

candidates.title: Die-casting Machine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for manufacturing once identical metal parts could be produced by forcing molten metal into a reusable mold?
candidates.notes: Doehler mass-produces metal parts.

candidates.title: Amplitude Modulation
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed the first time a human voice, rather than a telegraph signal, was broadcast over radio waves to ships at sea?
candidates.notes: Fessenden pioneers radio broadcasting.

candidates.title: Crystal Set Radio
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for ordinary households once a radio receiver could be built at home from cheap materials, needing no power source at all?
candidates.notes: Pickard brings broadcasts to the masses with a homemade receiver.

candidates.title: Triode
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for electronics once a weak radio signal could be amplified rather than merely rectified?
candidates.notes: De Forest creates the first valve amplifier.

candidates.title: Sonar
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about the safety of ships and submarines once sound echoes, rather than sight, could be used to detect what lay hidden underwater, and how did the sinking of the Titanic accelerate that adoption?
candidates.notes: Nixon uses echoes to pinpoint objects at sea.

candidates.title: Indicators / Electric Turn Signals
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for road safety once a driver's intention to turn could be signaled automatically instead of by hand?
candidates.notes: Douglas-Hamilton develops automatic signals.

candidates.title: Synthetic Detergent
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for household cleaning once a self-acting detergent could remove stains without rubbing or bleaching?
candidates.notes: Henkel introduces washing powder.

candidates.title: Distributor
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for multi-cylinder engines once high-voltage current could be automatically routed to the correct spark plug?
candidates.notes: Kent develops an ignition system.

candidates.title: Self-aligning Ball Bearing
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for machinery once a bearing could tolerate shaft misalignment without losing performance?
candidates.notes: Wingquist smooths mechanical movement.

candidates.title: Outboard Motor
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for recreational boating once a motor could simply be clamped onto the back of any rowboat?
candidates.notes: Evinrude speeds up pleasure boating.

candidates.title: Cellophane
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for food packaging once a transparent, waterproof, airtight film could be produced from plant cellulose?
candidates.notes: Brandenberger revolutionizes food packaging.

candidates.title: Food Mixer
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in home cooking once a lightweight motor could mix and beat ingredients at high speed?
candidates.notes: Beach speeds up kitchen tasks with a lightweight motor.

candidates.title: Geiger Counter
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for physics and later for public safety once ionizing radiation could be counted particle by particle?
candidates.notes: Geiger and Rutherford invent a device for detecting radiation.

candidates.title: Gyrocompass
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for navigation once a compass could point to true geographic north regardless of a ship's metal hull or magnetic fields?
candidates.notes: Anschütz-Kaempfe improves navigation at sea and in the air.

candidates.title: Coffee Filter
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in the daily ritual of coffee-making once grounds could be filtered out with disposable paper instead of settling or being strained?
candidates.notes: Bentz improves the coffee-making process.

candidates.title: Square-headed Screw
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for safety once a screw could guide the screwdriver into place and reduce the risk of it slipping?
candidates.notes: Robertson invents a safer and faster screw.

candidates.title: Washing Machine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Who could actually use the first electric washing machines, given that households wealthy enough to afford electricity often already had servants to do the laundry by hand?
candidates.notes: Fisher minimizes the physical work of the household washday.

candidates.title: Haber Process
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did it mean for both agriculture and warfare that the same chemical process could make ammonia plentiful enough to feed billions and to keep a country supplied with explosives?
candidates.notes: Haber makes ammonia readily available.

candidates.title: Bakelite
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for manufacturing once a fully synthetic material could be molded into any shape, ending reliance on natural shellac?
candidates.notes: Baekeland creates synthetic shellac.

candidates.title: Synthetic Rubber
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for industry once rubber no longer had to be harvested from trees but could be built up from simpler chemicals?
candidates.notes: Lebedev cooks up polybutadiene.

candidates.title: Fuel Injection
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What problem with carburetors did engineers hope fuel injection would eventually solve, decades before it became standard?
candidates.notes: Adams-Farwell does away with the choke.

candidates.title: Rayon
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for clothing once an artificial fiber could imitate silk at a fraction of the price?
candidates.notes: American Viscose Co. produces artificial silk.

candidates.title: Aluminum Foil
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for food preservation once thin sheets of aluminum could be rolled cheaply enough to replace tin as wrapping?
candidates.notes: J. G. Neher and Sons pioneer a new wrapping.

candidates.title: Infrared Photography
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became visible to surveyors, botanists, and astronomers once photography could capture light beyond what the human eye can see?
candidates.notes: Wood opens up the electromagnetic spectrum.

candidates.title: Depth Charge
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did navies have to develop once submarines made underwater attack possible and no effective countermeasure yet existed?
candidates.notes: Taylor develops the first effective antisubmarine weapon.

candidates.title: Neon Lamp
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in how cities advertised and displayed themselves once glowing colored gas tubes could be shaped into signs?
candidates.notes: Claude lights up the world with noble gases.

candidates.title: Starter Motor
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about the risk of simply owning a car once starting the engine no longer required hand-cranking that could injure or kill the driver?
candidates.notes: Kettering takes some labor out of motoring.

candidates.title: Knapsack Parachute
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Why were military governments reluctant to issue parachutes to their own pilots even after a device existed that could save their lives?
candidates.notes: Kotelnikov invents a safety device for pilots.

candidates.title: X-ray Crystallography
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became visible to scientists once X-rays could reveal the regular atomic arrangement inside a crystal?
candidates.notes: Von Laue and Ewald study crystal atoms.

candidates.title: Cloud Chamber
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became visible to physicists once the invisible paths of ionizing particles could be tracked as trails of condensed water droplets?
candidates.notes: Wilson discovers ionizing radiation.

candidates.title: MDMA (Ecstasy)
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: How did a compound first synthesized as a side product in a bleeding-control drug end up decades later fueling a billion-dollar illegal drug industry and organized crime?
candidates.notes: Köllisch happens upon a psychotropic drug.

candidates.title: Rotavator
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for soil quality once tilling could be powered by an engine rather than manual rotary tools?
candidates.notes: Howard develops a motorized rotary tiller.

candidates.title: Conveyor Belt
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in factory work once materials and parts could move continuously past stationary workers on a belt?
candidates.notes: Ford introduces the continuous moving band for transporting objects.

candidates.title: X-ray Tube
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for medical diagnosis once X-ray tubes could produce a stable, controllable beam safe enough for routine hospital and battlefield use?
candidates.notes: Coolidge develops a new diagnostic tool.

candidates.title: Zip Fastener
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for clothing manufacture once two rows of interlocking teeth could fasten a garment shut with one motion?
candidates.notes: Sundbäck invents a hookless fastening.

candidates.title: Stainless Steel
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for cutlery and industry once an iron alloy could resist rust and corrosion on its own?
candidates.notes: Brearley develops a “rustless” alloy.

candidates.title: Liquid Fuel Rocket
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What had to be proven, in the face of ridicule, before liquid-fueled rockets were taken seriously as a foundation for spaceflight?
candidates.notes: Goddard establishes modern rocketry.

candidates.title: Traffic Lights
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for pedestrians, cyclists, and drivers sharing unlegislated streets once a mechanical signal could impose the same stop-and-go rule on everyone?
candidates.notes: Morgan imposes a regulated control system on busy streets.

candidates.title: Military Tank
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about trench warfare once an armored, tracked vehicle could cross barbed wire and craters that had trapped infantry for years?
candidates.notes: The British Army finds a way to break through defended obstacles.

candidates.title: Oven-proof Glass
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible in the kitchen once glass could withstand oven heat without shattering?
candidates.notes: Sullivan and Taylor invent new cookware.

candidates.title: Lipstick
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in how lip color was applied and sold once it came in a portable sliding tube instead of a jar or paste?
candidates.notes: Levy puts lip color into a sliding tube.

candidates.title: Gas Mask
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: How quickly did armies have to adapt once poison gas was first used on the battlefield in 1915, and what did it take to build a mask that actually protected soldiers?
candidates.notes: Zelinsky filters toxic chemicals from air.

candidates.title: Tungsten Filament
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What made tungsten filament lightbulbs last far longer than the versions they replaced, and what everyday problem of blackening bulbs did that solve?
candidates.notes: Langmuir improves the lightbulb’s core.

candidates.title: Superheterodyne Receiver
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for tuning in specific radio stations once unwanted signals could be filtered out through frequency mixing?
candidates.notes: Armstrong improves radio technology.

candidates.title: Mass Spectrometer
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for chemistry, geology, and space science once atoms and molecules could be sorted and weighed by mass?
candidates.notes: Dempster devises an instrument essential to analysis of the physical world.

candidates.title: Hydraulic Brake
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Why were manufacturers slow to adopt hydraulic brakes even though they braked more evenly than mechanical systems, and what finally pushed Ford to switch in 1938?
candidates.notes: Lougheed uses fluid to improve braking.

candidates.title: Anthrax Vaccine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Who controlled access to a life-saving anthrax vaccine once its inventor refused for years to make the formula public, even under pressure from a government minister?
candidates.notes: Smith reveals a breakthrough medication.

candidates.title: Pivoting Bed
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for one-room city living once a bed could fold away into a closet during the day?
candidates.notes: Murphy improves one-room living with an ingenious space-saving bed.

candidates.title: Flip-flop Circuit
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for early computing once a circuit could hold onto one of two stable states, giving electronics a form of memory?
candidates.notes: Eccles and Jordan invent digital logic circuit.

candidates.title: Pop-up Toaster
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in the kitchen once a timer could automatically stop the toasting process and eject the bread?
candidates.notes: Strite makes burned toast a thing of the past.

candidates.title: Allen Key
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for assembling machinery and, later, flat-pack furniture once a single simple key could drive hexagonal screws?
candidates.notes: Unbrako (in the United States) and Brugola (in Italy) devise similar hexagonal drivers.

candidates.title: Jubilee Clip
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for sealing hoses and pipes once a tightening clip replaced wire whipping and split pins?
candidates.notes: Robinson firmly seals hoses and pipes.

candidates.title: Microelectrode
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: How many years of neurological research were lost because a woman scientist's invention of the microelectrode went unrecognized until after her death?
candidates.notes: Hyde facilitates the study of single cells.

candidates.title: BCG Vaccine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for controlling tuberculosis once a weakened, living strain of bacteria could be used to vaccinate people safely?
candidates.notes: Calmette and Guerin fight tuberculosis.

candidates.title: Lie Detector
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: How much authority should a machine measuring blood pressure and sweat have to identify a liar, given that the chapter itself notes there is no known physiological signal unique to lying?
candidates.notes: Larson identifies untruthful responses.

candidates.title: Refrigerator
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Why did the gas absorption refrigerator lose out to the electric refrigerator despite both being invented around the same time, and what does that say about how new household technologies get adopted?
candidates.notes: Von Platen and Munters develop a cooling cabinet for preserving food.

candidates.title: Blender
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in home and hospital kitchens once ingredients could be pureed by spinning blades instead of by hand?
candidates.notes: Poplawski shows the way to milkshakes and smoothies.

candidates.title: Snowmobile
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for winter travel and tourism once a tracked vehicle could cross snow that had previously required horse-drawn sleighs?
candidates.notes: Bombardier uses tracks to travel over snow.

candidates.title: Technicolor
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for filmmaking once movies could be shown in color, and why did it take a major studio's backing before the process became standard?
candidates.notes: Kalmus brings color to the movies.

candidates.title: Aga Cooker
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in home cooking once a cast-iron cooker could hold a steady heat from coke, and later other fuels, instead of an open fire?
