candidates.notes: Dalén produces an iconic kitchen appliance.

candidates.title: Water Ski
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What new recreational sport became possible once a person could be pulled across water on shaped boards behind a boat?
candidates.notes: Samuelson invents a glamorous new sport.

candidates.title: Cotton Buds
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened when a product marketed for decades as safe for cleaning ears was later found to risk perforating eardrums, forcing manufacturers to change their advice?
candidates.notes: Gerstenzang invents a swab on a stick.

candidates.title: Film Sound
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Why did Hollywood studios resist synchronized sound film even as competing, incompatible sound technologies were being developed, and what finally forced the industry to adopt it?
candidates.notes: De Forest ends the era of silent movies.

candidates.title: Bulldozer
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for earthmoving once a tracked tractor with a blade could do work that mules had done for backfilling trenches?
candidates.notes: Cummings introduces an earth-moving tractor to replace mule power.

candidates.title: Autogyro
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What flight risk did the autogyro's unpowered, auto-rotating design solve that fixed-wing aircraft could not, especially at low speed?
candidates.notes: De la Cierva paves the way for vertical flight.

candidates.title: Power Steering
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for drivers of heavy vehicles once steering no longer demanded significant physical strength?
candidates.notes: Davis and Jessup banish heavy steering.

candidates.title: Wind Tunnel
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for aircraft and automobile design once airflow at high altitude could be simulated on the ground?
candidates.notes: Munk invents realistic wind simulation.

candidates.title: Xenon Flash Lamp
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became visible to photographers once a flash of light could be timed to a millionth of a second, freezing motion invisible to the naked eye?
candidates.notes: Edgerton illuminates photography.

candidates.title: Iconoscope
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What had to happen technically before television could exist, and how long did it take for the necessary all-electric camera tube to reach American households?
candidates.notes: Zworykin paves the way toward television.

candidates.title: Fast-frozen Food
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about the taste and availability of preserved food once freezing could happen quickly enough to avoid large ice crystals damaging the texture?
candidates.notes: Birdseye freezes foods more quickly to preserve them in optimum condition.

candidates.title: Paper Tissues
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once consumers began using a product marketed for removing face cream as a disposable handkerchief instead, forcing the manufacturer to change its marketing?
candidates.notes: Kimberly-Clark creates paper hankies.

candidates.title: Ultracentrifuge
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became measurable about molecules once a centrifuge could spin fast enough to separate and weigh them by their rate of settling?
candidates.notes: Svedberg speeds up the centrifuge.

candidates.title: 35-mm Camera
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for photographers and the public once cameras became small and fast enough to capture spontaneous, unposed moments of history?
candidates.notes: Barnack's compact 35-mm camera made spontaneous, quick photography possible, jump-starting modern photojournalism.

candidates.title: Fluidized Bed Reactor
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible in fuel and plastics manufacturing once catalysts could be continuously regenerated in a fluidized bed?
candidates.notes: Winkler's fluidized bed reactor enabled continuous catalytic cracking, later used widely in fuel and polymer manufacturing.

candidates.title: Aerosol
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What regulatory and health reckonings followed once the aerosol can's propellants were found to damage the ozone layer and enable inhalant abuse?
candidates.notes: Rotheim's pressurized spray canister became ubiquitous but later drew scrutiny for solvent abuse, graffiti, and ozone-depleting CFCs.

candidates.title: Enigma Machine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once a code the Nazis considered unbreakable was cracked by spotting patterns in routine phrases?
candidates.notes: Scherbius's reflector-equipped Enigma was thought undecipherable, but British cryptologists found a flaw and cracked it.

candidates.title: Fluorescent Lamp
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in homes and workplaces once lighting could be produced more efficiently and with less heat than incandescent bulbs?
candidates.notes: Germer's fluorescent lamp offered cooler, more efficient lighting, with General Electric eventually dominating after patent disputes.

candidates.title: Television
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in daily life and shared public experience once moving images could be broadcast directly into people's homes?
candidates.notes: Farnsworth's all-electronic television system paved the way for a medium that came to dominate daily life and shared national moments.

candidates.title: PVC
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible in construction and consumer goods once a once-discarded waste chemical was turned into a versatile plastic?
candidates.notes: Semon's plasticized PVC turned a substance once thrown away into one of the world's most widely used plastics.

candidates.title: Iron Lung
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for polio patients and their families once a machine could keep them breathing until their own muscles recovered, and what happened to that dependency once a vaccine arrived?
candidates.notes: Drinker and Shaw's tank respirator kept paralyzed polio patients alive, a dependency that faded once the polio vaccine spread.

candidates.title: Chain Saw
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened to global forests and local industries once a hand-portable saw let a couple of workers fell trees at industrial speed?
candidates.notes: Stihl's portable chain saw sped up logging and wartime engineering but also enabled rapid deforestation worldwide.

candidates.title: Anodized Aluminum
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What new products became possible once aluminum could be given a hard, colorable, corrosion-resistant coating?
candidates.notes: Gower and O'Brien's anodizing process gave aluminum a tough, colorable protective oxide coating used in countless products.

candidates.title: Electric Razor
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in men's daily grooming routines once shaving no longer required water, soap, or a blade?
candidates.notes: Schick's electric razor freed users from the wet, bladed shaving ritual, though it took years to catch on commercially.

candidates.title: Bathysphere
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became visible about deep ocean life once humans could descend thousands of feet inside a pressure-proof sphere?
candidates.notes: Barton and Beebe's steel bathysphere let two explorers descend thousands of feet into the ocean, breaking depth records.

candidates.title: Freon
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What health trade-off did households accept when CFC refrigerants replaced toxic ammonia and sulfur dioxide, and what became of that trade-off once CFCs were found to be destroying the ozone layer?
candidates.notes: Midgley's Freon replaced dangerous refrigerants and enabled safe home refrigeration, until its ozone-depleting effects led to a global phase-out.

candidates.title: Automatic Bread Slicer
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in home baking and daily bread-eating habits once bread came pre-sliced and wrapped, ready to use?
candidates.notes: Rohwedder's slicing-and-wrapping machine drove a rapid consumer shift from unsliced to sliced bread within a few years.

candidates.title: Audiotape Recording
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for broadcasters and archivists once sound could be captured on reusable magnetic tape rather than fragile discs or wire?
candidates.notes: Pfleumer's magnetic-powder tape recording technique laid groundwork for the magnetophone and the postwar audio recording industry.

candidates.title: Color Television
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What took nearly two decades to change once color television was technically possible but too expensive and unfamiliar for most households to adopt?
candidates.notes: Baird's 1928 color television demonstration preceded a decades-long consumer adoption curve before color sets finally outsold black-and-white in 1972.

candidates.title: Barometric Altimeter
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for pilots once altitude could be measured accurately enough to fly safely through fog, clouds, and darkness?
candidates.notes: Kollsman's precision altimeter let pilots fly reliably 'by the gauges' in poor visibility, transforming aviation safety.

candidates.title: Cardiac Pacemaker
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Why did the inventor of the first artificial pacemaker keep a low profile about his device, and what changed once implantable pacemakers became routine decades later?
candidates.notes: Lidwell's early external pacemaker resuscitated a newborn but stayed obscure amid controversy over artificially extending life.

candidates.title: Electroencephalograph (EEG)
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did scientists need to see or believe before recording the electrical activity of a living human brain became acceptable, and why did Berger keep his early work secret?
candidates.notes: Berger secretly recorded the first human EEG, using lectures on telepathy as cover, before publishing work that revolutionized neurology.

candidates.title: Cyclotron
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What new physics became possible once scientists could generate a steady supply of high-energy particles rather than relying on scarce natural radioactive sources?
candidates.notes: Lawrence's cyclotron answered Rutherford's call for an abundant supply of high-energy particles, launching high-energy physics.

candidates.title: Antilock Braking System (ABS)
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened to real-world accident rates once ABS became standard, given that studies found many drivers didn't understand or correctly use the system?
candidates.notes: Voisin's antilock braking system, adapted from aircraft to cars, has had disputed real-world safety benefits due to driver misunderstanding.

candidates.title: Polarizing Filter
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for drivers, sunbathers, and wartime observers once glare could be selectively filtered out of light?
candidates.notes: Land's polarizing filters, first meant to cut headlight glare, found unexpected wartime use spotting submarines through binoculars.

candidates.title: Tampon with Applicator
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in women's daily freedom and activity once menstrual protection could be worn internally and discreetly, and what health risk did that change bring to light decades later?
candidates.notes: Haas's applicator tampon gave women new freedom and discretion, though it later raised toxic shock syndrome concerns.

candidates.title: Synchromesh Gears
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in who could drive confidently once cars no longer required the skill of double de-clutching to change gear smoothly?
candidates.notes: Cadillac's synchromesh gears eliminated the need for double de-clutching, making gear changes effortless for ordinary drivers.

candidates.title: Coaxial Cable
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible in long-distance communication once cables could carry high-frequency broadband signals without interference?
candidates.notes: Espenschied and Affel's coaxial cable design let signals travel with minimal interference, becoming vital communications infrastructure.

candidates.title: Polystyrene
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What packaging and construction habits became possible once a cheap, moldable plastic could be produced in bulk from crude oil?
candidates.notes: Wulff and Dorrer's economical polystyrene process enabled cheap mass production, later drawing environmental bans in some places.

candidates.title: Neoprene
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What activities and industries became possible once a synthetic rubber could match or exceed the properties of natural rubber?
candidates.notes: Carothers's neoprene became the first mass-produced synthetic rubber, later used widely in wetsuits, hoses, and industrial parts.

candidates.title: Image Intensifier
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for soldiers, astronomers, and doctors once faint or invisible light could be amplified tens of thousands of times into a visible image?
candidates.notes: Kubetsky's photomultiplier tube, refined by Zworykin, enabled night vision, astronomical observation, and medical imaging from otherwise undetectable light.

candidates.title: Tape
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What everyday problems of sealing and repair became easier once a reliable, all-purpose sticky tape existed?
candidates.notes: Drew's cellulose tape, developed to help seal cellophane food packaging, found uses far beyond what he originally imagined.

candidates.title: Radiosonde
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible in weather forecasting once instruments could transmit atmospheric data back to Earth in real time rather than relying on someone finding a fallen package?
candidates.notes: Molchanov's radiosonde let meteorologists receive continuous atmospheric data by radio instead of recovering instruments by chance.

candidates.title: Blind Rivet
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What construction problems were solved once fasteners could be installed with access from only one side of a material?
candidates.notes: Huck's blind rivet sped up aircraft assembly by allowing fastening from a single accessible side.

candidates.title: Radio Telescope
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became visible about the universe once astronomers could 'see' with radio waves instead of only visible light?
candidates.notes: Jansky's accidental discovery of cosmic radio static, made while investigating telephone interference, founded the field of radio astronomy.

candidates.title: Electric Guitar
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for musicians and audiences once the guitar could be heard over a full band, and why wasn't the instrument taken seriously for years after it was invented?
candidates.notes: Rickenbacker's electrically amplified guitar let the instrument be heard over loud bands, though it wasn't taken seriously until jazz virtuosos proved its potential.

candidates.title: Aerogel
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What new applications, from rocket fuel storage to comet-dust collection, became possible once a solid nearly as light as air could be manufactured?
candidates.notes: Kistler's aerogel, the lightest known solid, later found use as a thermal insulator and in space missions collecting comet dust.

candidates.title: Electron Microscope
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became visible to scientists once magnification was no longer limited by the wavelength of visible light?
candidates.notes: Ruska's electron microscope eventually exceeded the resolution of light microscopes, opening a new scale of scientific observation.

candidates.title: Stereo Sound
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in the cinema and recorded-music experience once sound could be made to 'follow' its visual source across two channels?
candidates.notes: Blumlein's binaural (stereo) recording system let sound position match an actor's location on screen.

candidates.title: Bourke Engine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Why did a patented, working engine design sit unused for decades even after its patents expired and anyone was free to build it?
candidates.notes: Bourke's radically simple two-piston engine was never adopted, whether from industry suppression, as its inventor believed, or genuine design flaws, as skeptics argue.

candidates.title: Anglepoise® Lamp
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in offices and workspaces once lighting could be precisely directed and repositioned without extra energy cost?
candidates.notes: Carwardine's spring-tensioned Anglepoise lamp, first designed for factory use, quickly proved ideal for offices and desks.

candidates.title: Folding Wheelchair
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened to the wheelchair market, and to the people who depended on it, once one company's folding design came to dominate the industry to the point of an antitrust suit?
candidates.notes: Everest and Jennings's folding X-brace wheelchair transformed mobility design but grew so dominant it drew a U.S. antitrust suit.

candidates.title: Sodium Thiopental
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What went wrong when a fast intravenous anesthetic developed for safer surgery was given in overdose to shocked trauma patients after Pearl Harbor, and how did the drug's later uses diverge from its medical origins?
candidates.notes: Volwiler and Tabern's sodium thiopental enabled safer intravenous anesthesia but was later misused in wartime trauma care and repurposed for interrogations and executions.

candidates.title: Parking Meter
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Who had to adjust once city streets began charging for the time a car occupied a parking space, and how did drivers contest that new authority?
candidates.notes: Magee's coin-operated parking meter addressed downtown congestion and generated local revenue, and the first ticketed driver immediately contested it in court.

candidates.title: Vinyl Phonograph Record
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Why did a technically superior recording format fail to catch on for two decades after its introduction, and what finally shifted listeners to it?
candidates.notes: RCA Victor's vinyl LP was technically superior to shellac discs but, launched amid the Great Depression, took roughly two decades to become dominant.

candidates.title: FM Radio
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in radio listening once broadcasts could avoid the interference and poor fidelity that had defined AM radio for decades?
candidates.notes: Armstrong's frequency modulation method eventually became the dominant means of high-fidelity broadcast, though adoption lagged well behind his patent.

candidates.title: Kitchen Extractor
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in home cooking and kitchen safety once smoke, grease, and odors could be actively vented rather than left to fill the house?
candidates.notes: Vent-a-Hood's kitchen extractor removed smoke and odors from home cooking, though early designs were themselves fire hazards.

candidates.title: Catseyes
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for drivers on unlit roads once a simple, self-cleaning reflective marker could show them the road's edge at night?
candidates.notes: Shaw's Catseye road marker, inspired by light reflecting off a cat's eyes, became a globally used, low-maintenance safety device.

candidates.title: Perspex®
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What new products and safety equipment became possible once a lightweight, shatter-resistant alternative to glass existed?
candidates.notes: Hill and Crawford's Perspex acrylic offered a lighter, stronger substitute for glass, used in aircraft canopies, visors, and medical devices.

candidates.title: Phillips Screw
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed on assembly lines once screws could self-center and avoid slipping under a powered screwdriver?
candidates.notes: Phillips's self-centering cross-head screw reduced slippage on automated production lines and sped up wartime vehicle manufacturing.

candidates.title: Trampoline
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in athletic training and military pilot conditioning once a portable bouncing frame could simulate disorientation and rebound practice?
candidates.notes: Nissen and Griswold's trampoline, built from spare materials in a garage, was later used by the military to condition pilots.

candidates.title: Electric pH Meter
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible in laboratory science once acidity could be measured precisely and immediately rather than estimated with litmus paper or fragile glass electrodes?
candidates.notes: Beckman's electric pH meter replaced unreliable litmus paper and fragile electrodes, letting scientists trust immediate, precise acidity readings.

candidates.title: Radar
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in wartime defense and later civilian life once distant objects could be detected and tracked by bouncing radio waves off them?
candidates.notes: Watson-Watt's radar, developed after a government request for a 'death ray' proved impossible, gave Britain an early-warning system before WWII.

candidates.title: Spectrophotometer
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became standardizable in industries like paint and dye once light intensity could be measured electronically instead of judged by eye?
candidates.notes: Hardy's spectrophotometer replaced the naked eye with photocells, enabling standardized measurement of color, pigments, and later atmospheric ozone.

candidates.title: Nylon
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened to fashion, wartime supply chains, and consumer demand once a synthetic fiber could substitute for silk that was becoming politically unavailable?
candidates.notes: Carothers's nylon, developed as trade tensions cut off Japanese silk, replaced silk in WWII parachutes and later created a massive stockings market.

candidates.title: Squeegee
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: How did an immigrant inventor overcome dealers who dismissed him by instead winning over the window cleaners who would actually use his tool?
candidates.notes: Steccone's squeegee, initially rejected by dealers, won over window cleaners directly and became the industry standard.

candidates.title: Epoxy Resin
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became buildable and repairable once an adhesive existed strong enough to bond aircraft parts and cure underwater?
candidates.notes: Castan and Greenlee independently developed epoxy resin, now used as a powerful adhesive and protective coating across industries.

candidates.title: Ski Lift
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in who could ski, and how often, once skiers no longer had to climb the mountain before skiing back down?
candidates.notes: Curran's chairlift, adapted from a banana-loading system, let skiers ride up the mountain instead of climbing, and was soon widely copied.

candidates.title: Suntan Lotion
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What social shift in beauty ideals and paid leisure time created demand for tanning products, and how long did it take before those products could actually be trusted to prevent skin cancer?
candidates.notes: Schueller's Bellis was the first sunscreen, created as tanned skin became fashionable, though effective cancer protection and SPF grading only came decades later.

candidates.title: Disposable Diapers
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Why did it take three separate inventors over two decades, and repeated rejection by companies, before disposable diapers became a mass-market product?
candidates.notes: Bruk's early paper diaper failed commercially; Donovan's nylon cover and later Mills's Pampers took over a decade more to establish disposable diapering as normal.

candidates.title: Biodiesel
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What alternative fuel source became scientifically established decades before petroleum scarcity or emissions concerns made it seem urgent?
candidates.notes: Chavanne's patented process for turning vegetable oil into diesel fuel predates today's push for renewable fuels by many decades.

candidates.title: Blood Bank
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible in treating trauma victims, in war and peacetime, once blood components could be separated, frozen, and stored for later use rather than needing an immediate donor?
candidates.notes: Drew's method of separating and preserving blood components enabled the first blood banks, scaled up dramatically to supply plasma for the British war effort.

candidates.title: Shopping Cart
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Why did shoppers initially refuse to use a cart that let them carry more, and what did the inventor have to do to change their minds?
candidates.notes: Goldman's shopping cart was initially shunned as unmasculine or stroller-like until he hired models of both sexes to normalize pushing one.

candidates.title: Jet Engine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in the speed, scale, and cost of air travel once propeller engines were replaced by jets developed independently on opposing sides of a war?
candidates.notes: Whittle and von Ohain independently developed jet engines that transformed both wartime air combat and, within a decade, commercial aviation.

candidates.title: Turboprop Engine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What kind of aircraft benefited once an engine could generate most of its thrust through a propeller rather than through the engine's own exhaust?
candidates.notes: Jendrassik's turboprop engine survived a troubled wartime debut to become standard in smaller, slower aircraft.

candidates.title: Ballistic Missile
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did it mean for civilians in London, Paris, and Antwerp once war could reach them from rockets fired hundreds of miles away with no warning, and what did the same technology later make possible?
candidates.notes: Dornberger's V-2 was used as a terror weapon against European civilians, and the same ballistic missile technology later carried humans into space.

candidates.title: Teflon®
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in cookware, industry, and consumer life once a substance was found that nothing else would stick to?
candidates.notes: Plunkett's accidental discovery of a slippery, heat-resistant polymer became Teflon, used in industry and, eventually, nonstick pans.

candidates.title: Fiberglass
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What new products, from car bodies to insulation, became possible once glass could be drawn into fine, flexible fibers at industrial scale?
candidates.notes: Slayter and Thomas's accidental discovery of glass-fiber spraying led to fiberglass insulation and, later, the fiberglass-bodied Corvette.

candidates.title: Walkie-talkie
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once two-way radios became small and rugged enough for a single person to carry and operate alone, moving from air-crash rescue to soldiers, police, and children at play?
candidates.notes: Hings's and Gross's portable two-way radios moved from wartime military use to policing and everyday civilian communication.

candidates.title: Lysergic Acid Diethylamide (LSD)
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in how society viewed a single chemical once it moved from psychiatric wonder drug used on thousands of patients to a symbol of 1960s countercultural rebellion?
candidates.notes: Hofmann's accidental self-experiment with LSD led to its use as a psychiatric treatment before it became associated with 1960s counterculture.

candidates.title: Kroll Process
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What military and aerospace applications became possible once a metal known to be strong and corrosion-resistant could finally be extracted in bulk?
candidates.notes: Kroll's process enabled bulk titanium production, later seized as enemy property under wartime law before enabling major aerospace industries.

candidates.title: Surround Sound
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What technical and economic obstacles kept immersive cinema sound from catching on for decades after Disney's first attempt?
candidates.notes: Disney's Fantasound was a costly, complex early surround-sound system that proved impractical for most theaters and was soon abandoned.

candidates.title: Cluster Bomb
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What international pressure built once cluster bombs' unexploded 'duds' and civilian casualties became widely documented, and why have major stockpiling nations still refused to sign a ban?
candidates.notes: Cluster bombs proved highly destructive but indiscriminate, prompting international pressure for a ban that major stockpiling nations have refused to join.

candidates.title: Helicopter
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in rescue, military, and transport operations once aircraft no longer needed a runway to take off or land?
candidates.notes: Sikorsky's VS-300 solved key stability problems that had plagued earlier helicopter designs, leading to widespread military use.

candidates.title: Semiconductor Diode
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible in radio and electronics once scientists understood that a 'flaw' in a cracked silicon crystal was actually a useful electrical junction?
candidates.notes: Ohl's accidental discovery of the p-n junction in cracked silicon laid the groundwork for the semiconductor diode and later the transistor.

candidates.title: DDT
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What public-health victories did DDT achieve against mosquito-borne disease, and what environmental reckoning led to its near-universal ban only three decades later?
candidates.notes: Muller's DDT eradicated malaria from entire islands before environmental concerns led to its near-universal ban by the early 1970s.

candidates.title: Silicone Rubber
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What options remained for tire, hose, and seal manufacturing once wartime shortages cut off the supply of natural rubber from Asia?
candidates.notes: Rochow's silicone rubber, invented amid a wartime natural-rubber shortage, became the basis of a new synthetic-rubber industry.

candidates.title: Penicillin Production
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What had to change in industrial fermentation before enough penicillin could be produced to treat Allied troops by D-Day, and what warning did Fleming issue even as this triumph was announced?
candidates.notes: Heatley's fermentation improvements scaled up penicillin production for WWII troops, even as Fleming warned in his Nobel address about coming antibiotic resistance.

candidates.title: Digital Electronic Computer
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did it mean to build the world's first program-controlled computer in a country isolated by war, with earlier versions repeatedly destroyed by bombing?
candidates.notes: Zuse built the first fully functional program-controlled digital computer in wartime isolation, after earlier machines were destroyed in Allied bombing raids.

candidates.title: Night Vision Goggles
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in nighttime military operations once soldiers could convert faint ambient light into a visible image?
candidates.notes: Spicer's night vision goggles used photoemission to amplify faint light into a visible image for nighttime military operations.

candidates.title: Bazooka
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened to anti-tank warfare once infantry could carry a shoulder-fired rocket launcher, and how quickly did opposing forces copy and adapt the design?
candidates.notes: The bazooka gave infantry an effective handheld anti-tank weapon, one Germany and later the Soviet Union quickly reverse-engineered after capturing examples.

candidates.title: Super Glue
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What emergency medical and forensic uses emerged for a laboratory adhesive originally meant for clear plastic gunsights?
candidates.notes: Coover's cyanoacrylate adhesive, developed for gunsights, was later used to seal battlefield wounds in Vietnam and to reveal fingerprints at crime scenes.

candidates.title: Bouncing Bomb
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What level of precision did pilots have to achieve, at what risk, once a weapon's success depended on skimming it across water at a very specific angle and height?
candidates.notes: Wallis's bouncing bomb exploited water-skimming physics to destroy heavily defended dams, requiring extremely low, precise bombing runs.

candidates.title: Kidney Dialysis
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for patients with kidney failure once toxins could be filtered from their blood by a machine, first improvised from sausage casings during wartime occupation?
candidates.notes: Kolff improvised the first dialysis machine using sausage-casing cellophane during wartime shortages, later expanding from emergency use to long-term treatment.

candidates.title: Aqualung
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in underwater exploration, filmmaking, and marine science once divers could move freely without a surface air line, and what military purpose motivated its invention?
candidates.notes: Cousteau and Gagnan's aqualung, developed partly to enable wartime frogman operations, transformed postwar underwater exploration and marine biology.

candidates.title: Disposable Catheter
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What infection risks changed once catheters could be manufactured cheaply enough to use once and discard, rather than cleaned and reused?
candidates.notes: Sheridan's disposable rubber catheter reduced infection risk compared to reused cotton catheters, driven partly by wartime supply shortages.

candidates.title: Electron Spectrometer
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became measurable about nuclear tests and space plasma once scientists could precisely track electron energy and trajectory?
candidates.notes: Deutsch and Evans's electron spectrometer, first used to monitor nuclear test radiation, later became a standard instrument on space missions.

candidates.title: Atomic Bomb
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: How did the relationships between nations change once a single weapon could threaten the kind of destruction the atomic bomb promised?
candidates.notes: The Manhattan Project's atomic bomb, built amid fears Nazi Germany might develop one first, permanently altered the balance of power between nations.

candidates.title: Cruise Control
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in the experience of long-distance driving once a car could hold a set speed without the driver's constant attention to the accelerator?
candidates.notes: Teetor's cruise control, inspired by his lawyer's jerky driving habits, let drivers set and maintain speed automatically.

candidates.title: Sofa Bed
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in how cramped urban apartments could be furnished once a sofa could easily transform into a bed and back again?
candidates.notes: Castro's easily convertible sofa bed helped cash-strapped city dwellers make better use of cramped apartment space.

candidates.title: Synchrotron
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible to study about the structure of matter once particle accelerators could reach ever-higher energies through synchronized magnetic and electric fields?
candidates.notes: McMillan and Veksler's synchrotron design, developed independently in the US and USSR, enabled ever-larger particle accelerators.

candidates.title: Microwave Oven
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in home cooking habits once food could be heated in minutes rather than through conventional cooking, and why did it take decades for consumers to trust and afford the device?
candidates.notes: Spencer's accidental discovery of microwave cooking led to bulky, expensive early ovens that consumers resisted before sales eventually overtook gas cookers.

candidates.title: Electronic Synthesizer
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What new kinds of musical expression became possible once sound could be shaped electronically and controlled by touch sensitivity rather than fixed acoustic properties?
candidates.notes: Le Caine's touch-sensitive electronic sackbut anticipated the voltage-controlled synthesizers that would shape popular music decades later.

candidates.title: Air-cushioned Sole
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: How did an orthopedic shoe sole designed to protect a doctor's injured joints end up as the symbol of choice for skinhead and punk subcultures?
candidates.notes: Maertens's air-cushioned orthopedic sole, invented after a skiing injury, was later adopted by postal workers and then youth subcultures as the Dr. Martens boot.

candidates.title: Citizens' Band Radio
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened when citizens began using CB radio equipment illegally before governments had even released the frequencies for legal use?
candidates.notes: Gross's citizens' band radio was often used illegally before governments released the frequencies, giving rise to its own trucker culture and slang.

candidates.title: Radial Tire
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What trade-offs did drivers and manufacturers accept once radial tires offered longer life and better handling but at higher manufacturing cost?
candidates.notes: Michelin's radial-ply tire outperformed bias-ply designs despite higher production costs, becoming the industry standard.

candidates.title: Tupperware®
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Why did a genuinely useful plastic container fail to sell in stores, and what change in how it was sold turned it into a household name?
candidates.notes: Tupper's grease-free, airtight plastic containers sold poorly in stores until the in-home 'Tupperware party' sales model transformed their popularity.

candidates.title: Chemotherapy
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What led doctors to turn a chemical weapon responsible for battlefield deaths into the first drug treatment for cancer?
candidates.notes: Gilman and Goodman's wartime research into mustard gas casualties led to nitrogen mustard becoming the first chemotherapy drug for cancer.

candidates.title: Acrylic Paint
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for artists once a fast-drying, durable paint became available for the first time since the fifteenth century?
candidates.notes: Bocour's Magna paint was the first significant new paint technology for artists since the Renaissance, valued for its durability and quick drying.

candidates.title: Transistor
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened to an entire generation of vacuum-tube technology once the transistor offered the same function with a fraction of the power, heat, and size?
candidates.notes: Bardeen, Shockley, and Brattain's transistor rendered valve technology largely obsolete within a decade of its 1947 demonstration.

candidates.title: Defibrillator
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in emergency response to cardiac arrest once an electric shock could restore a heart's rhythm outside of a hospital operating room?
candidates.notes: Beck's defibrillator, first used successfully on a boy whose heart stopped during surgery, evolved into today's public-access defibrillators.

candidates.title: Polaroid Self-developing Film Camera
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in the experience of photography once a picture could be seen within a minute of being taken, and what technology eventually made that instant gratification obsolete?
candidates.notes: Land's instant camera, inspired by his daughter's impatience to see a photo, dominated instant photography for decades before digital cameras ended production.

candidates.title: Radiocarbon Dating
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became newly verifiable about human and natural history once organic remains could be dated by measuring their radioactive carbon rather than by estimating from surrounding rock layers?
candidates.notes: Libby's radiocarbon dating replaced rough relative-dating methods, enabling precise dating of artifacts like the Dead Sea Scrolls.

candidates.title: Supersonic Airplane
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What had to be strengthened and redesigned in aircraft before pilots could safely fly faster than the speed of sound?
candidates.notes: Yeager's flight past Mach 1 required stronger airframes and more powerful jet engines to overcome the turbulence of the 'sound barrier.'

candidates.title: Multitrack Audio Recording
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible in music production once multiple performances could be layered together rather than captured in a single live take?
candidates.notes: Les Paul's overdubbing technique, first achieved with two wax-cylinder machines, led to multitrack tape recording adopted by major studios.

candidates.title: Barcode
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Why did it take years after the barcode was invented before affordable lasers and computers made it practical to use at scale?
candidates.notes: Silver and Woodland's barcode combined movie-soundtrack and Morse code techniques to create automated product tracking, though practical scanners lagged for years.

candidates.title: Holography
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became visible once light itself could be encoded to store a three-dimensional image, and what invention decades later finally made that vision reliably reproducible?
candidates.notes: Gabor's holography concept was hampered by weak light sources until the laser's invention enabled practical, reproducible 3D images.

candidates.title: Weather Radar
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became forecastable about storms and precipitation once radar, originally built to detect enemy aircraft, was redirected at the weather itself?
candidates.notes: Weather radar repurposed wartime aircraft-detection technology to measure rainfall, storm movement, and turbulence.

candidates.title: Cable Television
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What began as one shopkeeper's fix for neighbors who couldn't get a TV signal because of nearby mountains, and how did that local solution grow into infrastructure used in most American homes?
candidates.notes: Walson's mountaintop antenna, built to solve his own customers' poor TV reception, grew into the community antenna system that became modern cable television.

candidates.title: Robot
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What did simple electro-mechanical 'tortoises' reveal about the origins of lifelike behavior in neural systems?
candidates.notes: Walter's tortoise robots, Elmer and Elsie, used simple circuitry to mimic lifelike behavior, helping found the sciences of cybernetics and robotics.

candidates.title: Ice Rink Cleaning Machine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in how ice rinks operated once resurfacing could be done by one person in minutes instead of three people over ninety minutes?
candidates.notes: Zamboni's ice resurfacer automated a job that previously took three workers ninety minutes, doing it with one operator in ten.

candidates.title: Synthetic Zeolites
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What industrial and agricultural uses became possible once zeolites could be manufactured pure and uncontaminated rather than mined from volcanic deposits?
candidates.notes: Barrer's synthetic zeolites offered purer, more uniform molecular sieves than natural deposits, used in water treatment, agriculture, and nuclear fuel processing.

candidates.title: Acetaminophen
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What safety concerns about existing painkillers drove the search that produced acetaminophen, and how did that safety record reshape which pain relievers people trusted?
candidates.notes: Axelrod and Brodie discovered acetaminophen while investigating blood-poisoning risks from another painkiller, and it was marketed as a safer alternative to aspirin.

candidates.title: Ventilator
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What forms of surgery and injury became survivable once machines could take over breathing for a paralyzed or incapacitated patient?
candidates.notes: Emerson's mechanical ventilator, developed amid polio epidemics and rising use of paralyzing anesthetic drugs, kept patients breathing when they otherwise could not.

candidates.title: Atomic Clock
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible to track, from satellite positioning to continental drift, once time could be measured to an accuracy of one second in three million years?
candidates.notes: Essen's caesium atomic clock redefined the second itself, underpinning GPS satellites and precise geophysical measurements.

candidates.title: Centrifugal Clutch
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in operating small engines like scooters and chainsaws once a clutch could engage automatically based on engine speed alone?
candidates.notes: Fogarty's centrifugal clutch, born of frustration with his motor scooter, automated gear engagement in lightweight engines.

candidates.title: Intraocular Lens
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Why did the medical community initially reject the idea of leaving an artificial lens inside a patient's eye, and what changed to make it a routine operation performed millions of times a year?
candidates.notes: Ridley's intraocular lens, inspired by inert Perspex shards observed in wounded pilots' eyes, faced scornful medical skepticism before becoming routine cataract treatment.

candidates.title: Pager
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Why did doctors initially resist carrying a device meant to reach them in emergencies, and what changed to make it indispensable to the medical profession?
candidates.notes: Gross's pager was first resisted by doctors annoyed by its beeping before becoming an essential hospital tool, though his patents expired before he could profit from its later popularity.

candidates.title: Crash Test Dummy
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What could safety engineers finally measure repeatedly and systematically once crash test dummies replaced human cadavers in impact testing?
candidates.notes: Alderson's crash test dummies replaced the use of human cadavers in safety testing, enabling repeatable measurement of impact forces for car and aircraft design.

candidates.title: Magnetic Core Memory
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in how much people trusted computers to store important records once memory could reliably retain data even after power was cut?
candidates.notes: Wang and Woo's magnetic core memory gave early computers reliable, persistent data storage for the first time.

candidates.title: Credit Card
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: How did societies' relationship with debt change once paying with borrowed money became as easy as handing over a plastic card, and why did adoption lag in countries with less trusted banking systems?
candidates.notes: McNamara's credit card system was embraced quickly in developed countries but adopted more slowly where banking systems were less trusted, and later fueled concerns about unsustainable consumer debt.

candidates.title: Television Remote Control
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in television viewers' relationship to advertising once they could mute or change the channel without leaving their chair?
candidates.notes: Zenith's remote control, invented partly to let viewers 'tune out annoying commercials,' evolved through several technologies before settling on infrared.

candidates.title: Tokamak
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What promise of clean, abundant energy did nuclear fusion research raise, and how far short of that promise has progress fallen in the decades since?
candidates.notes: Sakharov and Tamm's tokamak design aimed to harness nuclear fusion's promise of clean energy, though practical fusion power has progressed slowly.

candidates.title: Nuclear Reactor
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What had to change, institutionally and in public purpose, once the same nuclear chain reaction that powered the Manhattan Project was redirected toward generating electricity for civilian use?
candidates.notes: Zinn, who had built the first self-sustaining nuclear reaction for the Manhattan Project, later led the reactor design that produced the first electricity from nuclear power.

candidates.title: Hydrogen Bomb
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in the scale of destructive power nations held once fission bombs, already devastating, were dwarfed by a design hundreds of times more powerful?
candidates.notes: Teller and Ulam's hydrogen bomb design was hundreds of times more powerful than WWII atomic bombs, prompting Einstein's warning about the future of warfare.

candidates.title: Liquid Paper
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What happened to a secretary's job once her side invention for covering typing mistakes grew successful enough that her employer fired her for using company paper to promote it?
candidates.notes: Graham's Liquid Paper began as a homemade correction fluid shared with office colleagues and grew into a multi-million-dollar company after she was fired from her secretarial job.

candidates.title: Tetra Pak
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in how far and how cheaply perishable foods like milk and juice could travel once aseptic packaging removed the need for refrigeration?
candidates.notes: Rausing and Wallenberg's Tetra Pak used aseptic sterilization and layered packaging to extend shelf life and enable cheaper, refrigeration-free transport of dairy and juice.

candidates.title: Optical Fiber
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once light could carry information through glass fibers instead of copper wires?
candidates.notes: Kapany pioneers the use of fiber optics for medicine and telecommunications.

candidates.title: Bubble Chamber
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became visible to physicists once subatomic particles could leave visible trails in a chamber of liquid?
candidates.notes: Glaser advances the study of particle physics.

candidates.title: Air Bag
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What had to change for manufacturers, regulators, and drivers before airbags went from a style-conscious industry's low priority to a mandatory standard feature?
candidates.notes: Hetrick’s invention saves lives in automobile accidents.

candidates.title: Polio Vaccine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for families once a vaccine could prevent the disease that had paralyzed thousands of children each year?
candidates.notes: Salk develops a life-saving injectable vaccine.

candidates.title: Cloning
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in scientists' understanding of development once an adult cell's nucleus could be shown to direct the growth of a whole new organism?
candidates.notes: Briggs and King genetically copy organisms.

candidates.title: Roll-on Deodorant
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in a decades-old consumer product once inspiration from an unrelated invention, the ballpoint pen, gave it a new applicator?
candidates.notes: Diserens invents easily applicable deodorant.

candidates.title: Speech Recognition
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible, and what were the limits, once a machine could try to recognize human speech instead of only processing typed input?
candidates.notes: Bell creates computers that recognize speech.

candidates.title: Hovercraft
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What kinds of terrain and cargo became newly accessible once a craft could travel on a cushion of air across both land and water?
candidates.notes: Cockerell invents a craft that floats on air.

candidates.title: Heart-Lung Machine
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What risks did patients and surgeons accept during the decades it took to make a machine reliably take over the heart's work during surgery?
candidates.notes: Gibbon’s machine is a major breakthrough for heart surgery.

candidates.title: Adaptive Optics
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What could astronomers finally see clearly once a mirror could correct for the atmosphere's distortion of starlight in real time?
candidates.notes: Babcock comes up with an optical system to aid astronomers.

candidates.title: WD-40®
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once a rust-prevention chemical developed for the aerospace industry found its way into ordinary households?
candidates.notes: Larsen invents product with unimagined uses.

candidates.title: Synthetic Diamond
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed once diamonds could be manufactured under secrecy rather than mined, and what happened when a rival team went public first?
candidates.notes: Von Platen achieves diamond alchemy.

candidates.title: Black Box Flight Recorder
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Who gained the authority to reconstruct a plane's final moments once cockpits began recording themselves, and what finally made regulators require it?
candidates.notes: Warren’s box is a major step forward for the safety of air travel.

candidates.title: Backhoe Loader
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What construction tasks became easier once a single machine could combine a loader and a digging arm on one tractor?
candidates.notes: Bamford invents a powerful, versatile piece of construction equipment.

candidates.title: Felt-tip Pen
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed about where and how people could write once ink no longer depended on a nib or stylus?
candidates.notes: Rosenthal’s pen leaves an indelible mark.

candidates.title: Medical Ultrasonography
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became visible inside a beating heart, and later inside the womb, once doctors could use sound waves instead of surgery or X-rays to look?
candidates.notes: Edler and Hertz advance medical imaging.

candidates.title: Geodesic Dome
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible to build once a dome could be assembled from self-reinforcing triangles instead of traditional load-bearing walls?
candidates.notes: Fuller creates an architectural form from patterns of reinforcing triangles.

candidates.title: Automatic Doors
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What everyday expectation changed once doors began opening themselves, to the point that a door that doesn't open automatically now causes momentary confusion?
candidates.notes: Horton and Hewitt introduce a new door system to the world.

candidates.title: Non-Stick Pans
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in the kitchen once an industrial coating originally used on aluminum and fishing gear was adapted for cookware?
candidates.notes: Marc and Colette Grégoire create an ingenious kitchen utensil.

candidates.title: Transistor Radio
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in how and where people listened to music and news once radios became small, portable, and private enough to carry anywhere?
candidates.notes: Texas Instruments produce the first radio in miniature.

candidates.title: Polypropylene
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What products became possible once a stronger, lighter plastic could be made using a new class of catalysts?
candidates.notes: Natta and Ziegler create one of the world’s most important plastics.

candidates.title: SI Units
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became easier to compare, trade, and coordinate internationally once most of the world adopted a single common system of units, and why have a few countries still not adopted it?
candidates.notes: The Committee for Weights and Measures introduces a universal system of measurement.

candidates.title: Breathalyzer
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed for police and courts once intoxication could be measured with a number instead of relying only on an officer's observation of a suspect?
candidates.notes: Borkenstein invents a device to deter driving under the influence of alcohol.

candidates.title: Ventouse
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Why did an alternative to forceps delivery take decades to gain acceptance, and what changed once later reports linked it to serious complications?
candidates.notes: Malmström invents a device to assist birth.

candidates.title: Gel Electrophoresis
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What became possible for scientists once proteins could be separated and compared by size using a simple starch-gel sieve?
candidates.notes: Smithies discovers a molecular sieve.

candidates.title: Velcro
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What changed in fastening clothing and gear once a two-sided hook-and-loop fabric, inspired by burrs stuck to a dog's fur, replaced zippers in many uses?
candidates.notes: Mestral invents a unique fastening material inspired by nature.

candidates.title: Speed Camera
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: Who gained the authority to enforce speed limits automatically once cameras could record and fine drivers without an officer present, and why did many drivers see this as unfair?
candidates.notes: Gatsonides’s device reduces traffic accidents.

candidates.title: Hair Spray
candidates.possibleSocialAdjustmentQuestion: What had to change in a popular product's chemistry once its propellant was linked to ozone depletion?
candidates.notes: Chase Products’ spray holds hair in place.

candidates.title: Tetracycline
